# Preface to the Reader.

In accordance with your status, honored reader, that I have written this has happened out of the compassion I have toward my neighbor. I know what trouble I have had because of the obscure writings in the good <term>chemical books</term> <note>In the 18th century, "chemical" (chymisch) almost always referred to what we now call alchemy—the pursuit of the Philosopher's Stone and the transmutation of metals.</note>; nor is there a good friend to be found in the entire world who might instruct one. The greatest damage and hindrance arises especially from the fact that many <term>will-o'-the-wisps</term> <note>original: "Irrwische". A metaphor for charlatans or "sophists" who lead seekers into "swamps" of error with false or misleading instructions.</note> are found who write about this matter, yet know nothing of it themselves and lead one astray through their narratives; even when one has already found their way a bit, they lead one back onto wrong paths. Some have written so "learnedly" and obscurely about the matter that no person is meant to understand it, because they did not understand themselves, nor did they know what they were writing about; those who can do nothing but prattle about common gold (☉) and silver (☽), or of iron (♂), copper (♀), tin (♃), lead (♄), and mercury (☿), to which bod- <note>The word is interrupted by the page break; it refers to "bodies" (Cörper), the physical substances used in alchemical work.</note>

<summary>In this preface, the author explains that his book is born of empathy for students frustrated by the intentional obscurity of alchemical literature and the deceptions of ignorant charlatans. He criticizes those who speak only of common metals without true philosophical understanding.</summary>
<keywords>alchemy, charlatanism, hermetic philosophy, planetary symbols, metals, chemical books, pedagogical compassion</keywords>

The contents of this book are composed in five chapters according to the nature of the work, which is illustrated in the five circles and in the five tables. These tables explain the five chapters and demonstrate the work: the **old long path** and the **new short path** <note>In alchemy, the "Long Path" (Via Humida) usually refers to a slow, gradual process involving glass vessels and low heat, while the "Short Path" (Via Sicca) is a faster, more intense process using crucibles and high heat.</note>.

**Secrets to be found regarding this matter, contained within the five chapters.**

I. **Hermetic Brass** <note>original: *Æs Hermetis*. A symbolic name for the base metal or the raw material used at the start of the work.</note>, the **subject of nature** <note>original: *subjectum der Natur*. The specific substance chosen to undergo the transformation.</note>, the first **confused chaos**, **remote matter** <note>original: *materia remota*. The substance in its raw, unrefined state before it is prepared for the Great Work.</note>, the **matter of our Stone** <note>original: *materia Lapidis nostri*.</note>. Is it **Saturn** <note>The symbol ♄ represents Saturn, which in alchemy is almost always associated with the metal lead or the "black" stage of the process.</note> purified like **Magnesia**, cleansed of its **dregs** <note>original: *fecibus*. Impurities or sedimentary waste.</note> according to nature, brought into **prime matter** <note>original: *primam Materiam*. The formless, original state of all matter.</note>, and into its first water; is the **vitriol** <note>A term for various metal sulfates, highly prized for their corrosive and transformative properties.</note> dissolved in its own previous waters?

II. How to make the **viscous, heavy water** or the **simple Mercury** <note>The symbol ☿ represents Mercury/Quicksilver.</note> from these?

III. How the **double Mercury** <note>original: *☿ duplicatus*. A more refined or "philosophical" mercury combined with another principle.</note> is made from this **Virgin’s Milk** <note>original: *Jungfer-Milch*. A common alchemical metaphor for a white, nourishing liquid or solvent produced during the process.</note>; the first composition toward the **foliated earth** <note>original: *terra foliata*. A stage where the matter begins to crystallize into leaf-like layers.</note>?

IV. How this **volatile bird** <note>A metaphor for a substance that vaporizes or sublimes easily when heated.</note> is to be bound by the **strongest fire** <note>original: *ignis fortissimus*.</note>, so that it becomes the **white stone**, the **white tincture**, the **stone of the first order**?

V. How this is made yellow and brought to the **highest redness**? How this is to be **multiplied** (which is the **subject of the art**), and how all these spring from the single one, requiring nothing but **dissolution** <note>original: *Solution*.</note> and **coagulation**, with nothing foreign added?

Our **matter** is only one thing, and yet it has the number 1, 2, 3, 4. Specifically: 1. One thing in **reality and in number** <note>original: *re & numero*. Existing as a single physical entity.</note>. 2. Man and Woman. 3. The content of this book is organized into 5 chapters according to the nature of the Work, which is depicted in the 5 circles and the 5 tables. These tables explain the 5 chapters and demonstrate the process, covering both the "old long path" and the "new short path" <note>In alchemy, the "long path" (via longa) usually involves slower, more traditional methods, while the "short path" (via brevis) suggests a more direct or intense procedure.</note>.

Secrets to be found within this Matter, contained in the 5 chapters:

I. Hermetic Brass <note>original: "Æs Hermetis"</note>, the subject of Nature, the first "confused Chaos," the remote matter, the matter of our Stone; it is Saturn <note>The symbol ♄ refers to the metal Lead, which alchemists believed was the "starting point" for gold</note> refined like Magnesia <note>A term alchemists used for the crude, unrefined "body" of their matter</note>, purified of its dregs <note>original: "fecibus"</note> according to Nature, brought into the Prime Matter <note>original: "primam Materiam"</note>, and into its first water—is the vitriol dissolved in its own previous waters?

The first Chaos of Nature, dissolved Mercury <term>☿ solut.: dissolved mercury, often representing the volatile spirit</term>. ### Description of the 1st Circle, regarding its name.

The first chaos of nature, dissolved mercury <note>symbol: ☿; original: *solut*</note>, Hermetic bronze <note>original: *Es Hermetis*</note>, *magnesia*, *immature mineral electrum* <note>a natural alloy of gold and silver</note>, *mercury of the philosophers* <note>original: ☿ *Philosophorum*</note>, the showing-father of all gods, containing the *prime matter* <note>original: *prima materia*</note> of all metals, the *coagulated mercury* <note>original: ☿ *coagulatus*</note>, the great alkali, the *prime metal* <note>original: *metallum primum*</note>, the *crude mercury of the philosophers* <note>original: ☿ *crudus Philosophophorum*</note>, the rock that gives oil, wine, blood, and milk; the gold tree and its root, the beginning and the end, one thing *in reality and in number* <note>original: *Re & Numero*</note>.

### Description of the Purification.

Lead our "Old One" into his bath of purification, and you will have a secret. Take our Old One, who has played so much with Venus <note>symbol: ♀; here representing copper or perhaps worldly desire</note> and has therefore become impure, who has the *prime metal* <note>original: *metallum primum*</note>, the coral-red juice within himself; he who has the gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> hidden in his body, or our gold which lies locked in its dungeon and is called the *red lion* <note>symbol: ♌; original: *rubeus*</note>; dissolve him in nature's own vinegar.

### Division into the fixed and the volatile.

You should by no means dissolve the entire body <note>original: *corpus*</note>, but only its soul <note>original: *animam*</note>. Take all of its blood, the "red nut," in which our Mars [♂], Venus [♀], Sun [☉], and Moon [☽]—indeed, all seven metals—are hidden. Take from this man, while he sleeps, his wife, his rib <note>original: *Riebe*, likely meaning rib (*Rippe*) in reference to the creation of Eve</note>; distill the volatile wife, the poisonous salt-water, from him. In this way, you will find at the bottom the red clay, the <term>Adamic earth [terram Adamicam]</term> which is so close to Paradise, the red antimony [♁], our cinnabar ore.

### Names of this water or spirit, and of the fixed part.

This water is called the "received gift of God," "mountain vinegar," "dissolving water," "poisonous snake" or "dragon," "Juno," "raw immature spirit of Mercury [☿]," "the snake lying in the green grass," "May dew," and "distilled vinegar." The fixed part, representing the man, is called our Sun [☉], the Gold of GOD, and our Sun [☉] and Moon [☽] tree, which bears the red and white Sun [☉] and Moon [☽] flowers. This must be dissolved in its own moisture, its own water, so that the white and red substances may come to light.

### Description of the Second Circle.

Make a Sun [☉] <note>symbol for Gold or the solar principle</note> out of man and woman; combine our matter, both the volatile and the fixed, which signifies man and woman. This is the poisonous snake that dissolves our secret salt [$\ominus$] <note>original: *salvirt*</note>. It comes from Saturn [♄] and is indeed Saturn [♄], who swallowed a stone instead of his son Jupiter [♃] and spat it out again. It is also the eagle-stone <note>original: *Adler-Stein*; a hollow stone believed to have magical properties</note> which contains another stone within it—namely, the Philosopher's Stone. By visiting the interior of the earth and by rectifying, you will find the hidden stone, the true medicine <note>original: *Visitando Interiora Terræ Rectificando Invenies Occultum Lapidem Veram Medicinam*; the initials of this Latin phrase form the word "VITRIOL," a key alchemical substance</note>. This is our generating vitriol, which contains within itself the red and white spirit: the red man and the white woman. It dissolves through its own water, for it is said: It dissolves itself, and it turns itself black, white, and red, etc. Now our confused chaos <note>original: *confusum Chaos*</note> is formed, in which the elements lie hidden and from which the many solvents <term>menstrua [the liquid agents used to dissolve or transform solids]</term> emerge.

However, these solvents are not seen until it pleases the artist <note>the alchemist</note>, who must bring them to light—that is, separate them into the elements. From these, two columns are made, upon which the entire building of the work rests. Herein are contained the preliminary works of Hercules—his twelve labors. The <term>Rebis [the "double-thing," a hermaphroditic figure representing the union of opposites]</term> is but a single thing, yet prepared from two things; Sun and Moon <note>symbolizing Gold and Silver, or the masculine and feminine principles</note> are dissolved so that one may have their first seed. ### Description of the Third Circle.

Make a <term>square [□]</term> <note>symbolizing the four elements: Earth, Air, Fire, and Water</note> out of man and woman; divide it into the four elements. It is commonly called the Elixir, the other well-known part of the work, in which the beautiful bodies are purely and finely turned into water. The Elixir is a tincturing water, a <note>original: *venenum tingens*</note> staining poison, our snow-white incombustible <term>Sulfur [🜍]</term>, and our blood-red fixed <term>Sulfur [🜍]</term>: the white spirit for the white work, the red spirit for the red work, heat from the Sun, saliva from the Moon, and solar <term>Sulfur [🜍]</term>.

From a rock, God gave clear water, and a quantity of oil from a hard stone. When the elements are separated, the air appears yellow and is fatty like oil; this is the Sages' <note>original: *spiritus vini*</note> spirit of wine <note>a high-proof alcohol used as a solvent</note>, because it dissolves all <term>Sulfurs [🜍]</term> and carries them over the <note>original: *Helm*</note> alembic <note>the cap of a still used for distillation</note>. It is also called the <term>Spirit of Mercury [☿]</term>, and without this, no <term>potable gold [aurum potabile]</term> <note>a legendary medicine made of dissolved gold</note> can be made; it tints all bodies yellow, which is to say, into <term>Gold [☉]</term>.

The water is called Virgin’s Milk, Virginal <term>Mercury [☿]</term>, Pheasant, Swan, and the <note>original: *menstruum mundi*</note> solvent of the world.

### Description of the Fifth Circle.

Make out of man and woman a **Gold [☉]** once more; when you join the head to the tail <note>a reference to the Ouroboros, the serpent eating its own tail, symbolizing the completion of a cycle</note>, then you have the **Tincture** <term>Tinctur; a potent substance capable of transforming base metals into gold</term> whole. Then the world, which remained from the **Great Flood** <note>original: *Sündfluth*</note>, is now judged through fire; thus the **new heaven and the new earth** will appear, which remains eternally and is subject to no change. Our **Carbuncle** <term>Carfunkel; a mythical gemstone said to emit its own light</term>, which shines in the dark, the **Salamander**, which lives in the fire, unburnable oil, eternal light.

From man and woman, make a circle [◯] once more; bring man and woman together. When you have brought the white woman to the red man, they shall immediately accept one another in friendship; thereupon the noble white woman conceives. Those who previously were two have become but one body. Stone of the first order.

For a better explanation of the five circles and five tables, and as a repetition of the preliminary work, the twelve labors of Hercules are set forth. <note>In alchemical literature, the Twelve Labors of Hercules were often interpreted as allegories for the different chemical processes required to create the Philosopher's Stone.</note>

1. The first labor shows us the **raw and remote matter** <note>original: *Materiam crudam & remotam*</note>, namely Saturn [♄] <note>The planet and deity associated with the metal Lead, often representing the heavy, unrefined starting material</note>. This comes from Juno—that is, the metallic nature has sent down two snakes, one volatile and one fixed, which are contained within a single subject and are poisonous. We must take these in their raw state, just as nature gives them to us, without any foreign addition; this is our **Rebis** <note>original: *Rebis*; from the Latin *res bina* ("double thing"), a symbol of the union of opposites like male/female or spirit/matter</note>.

2. The second labor shows us the Vitriol [⊕] <note>The symbol ⊕ here refers to the "proximate matter" or the refined earth</note>—the **proximate matter** <note>original: *Materiam propinquam*</note>, our **confused chaos** <note>original: *confusum Chaos*</note>. This occurs when the matter is in the state of putrefaction <note>the stage of decay or "blackening" necessary for rebirth</note>, and the Sun and Moon still lie hidden in their dark shadows. These [the Sun and Moon] are present, but they cannot be seen until it pleases the artist <note>the alchemist</note>, who must bring them to light.

The many-colored hues are not seen until after the blackness, when the *matter* [original: materia] begins to become dry. If the moist vapors were active, one would see the many-colored hues sooner, which scatter about the glass like subtle **glittering scales** [original: Geflinder], because the wind must carry them entirely in its belly <note>a reference to the *Emerald Tablet* of Hermes Trismegistus, a foundational alchemical text: "The wind carried it in its belly, the earth is its nurse"</note>. When the green color reveals itself, the reign of **Venus** arrives. Just as the **Moon**, when it first resolves <note>original: *resolvirt*; dissolves or melts</note> into its "first water" in the mines, becomes a descending ore and **Venus** [copper] comes from it; so it is here also. You must moisten this earth at the right time with its water; if it becomes too dry and receives more fire than belongs to it, you are in great danger. The stone also indicates to you by its color if it is becoming too hot; if it turns red like a wild poppy or the flesh-color of a human, then the stone is in the agony of death. Immediately soak this earth with the <term>Water of Life</term>, with its <term>Virgin's Milk</term> <note>alchemical terms for the specialized solvent or "mercurial water" used to nourish the Stone</note>; refresh it in its thirst so that it comes back to itself, because its spirit already wanted to flee from it. 

When the reign of **Venus** has come to an end, and it has been awakened again by the <term>crack of resolution</term> <note>original: *Resolutions-Knall*; likely a physical sound or popping reaction within the glass vessel as the matter changes state</note>, then this **Mercury**—which is already skillful enough—wants to cook itself into **Sol** <note>symbol ☉; gold</note>. ### Of Particulars
<note>"Particulars" refers to smaller alchemical processes intended to produce a specific result, like changing a small amount of metal, rather than the "Universal" medicine or the Great Work.</note>

However, these are only small branches, which do not tint <note>transform the color and nature of a substance</note> nearly as highly as the Great Work.

Yet another way: One **dissolves** <note>original: "solvirt"</note> **mercury** in **acid-water** <note>original symbol: "🜄"</note>, draws it over again <note>distills it</note>, pours another **acid-water** upon it, and draws it over again until the **mercury** turns red. Upon this, one pours the aforementioned **tinting drops**, which it swallows up. This can be done several times until the **precipitate** <note>the solid substance that settles out of the liquid</note> is of the most beautiful color and **fixed** <note>meaning it is stable and will not evaporate when heated</note>. One mixes this with wax and throws it in small pieces into **silver** while it is in **flux** <note>melted in the crucible</note>, or uses it to **cement** <note>a process of heating a metal with a powdered reagent to purify or color it</note> the **silver** with it.

93. The easiest and best **Grading-Water** <note>a liquid used to improve or "grade" the purity and color of metals, often to give them the appearance or properties of gold</note> is made in this way with little expense: **iron** filings <note>original symbol: "♂"</note>, **verdigris** <note>a green pigment/chemical formed on copper</note>, yellow **vitriol** <note>original symbol: "⊕"</note>, **pyrite**, **solar iron ore** <note>original: "minera martis solaris"; likely hematite or a specific iron sulfide</note> in round pieces, **yellow realgar** <note>original: "Sulph. rausch gelb"; a toxic arsenic sulfide mineral</note>, and **orpiment** <note>original: "auripigment"; another arsenic sulfide</note>. These last two are used with diligence because they contain much **arsenic**, which seizes the **sulfur** <note>original: "Sulph."</note> and carries it upward. However, common **sulfur** must make up the majority. Put these well-powdered into a **retort** <note>a glass vessel with a long downward-pointing neck used for distillation</note> and distill it with the strongest heat. A little water will rise over; the rest is a **sublimate** <note>a solid deposit from the vapors</note> of **sulfur** and **iron**, appearing like a red glass when it has had enough fire. One opens the **dead head** <note>original: "Caput mortuum"; the nutrient-depleted residue left in the retort</note> even better by **subliming** it with an equal weight of **sal ammoniac** <note>original symbol: "∗"</note>. This beautiful **sublimate** and the previous one are mixed, when ground as fine as possible, with four times its weight of **gold** <note>original symbol: "☉"</note> and four times its weight of **calcined vitriol** <note>original symbol: "⊕"; vitriol heated until it becomes a dry powder</note>. Distill this into a **receiver** <note>original: "Vorlage"</note> in which the previous water has already been collected. However, it must be mixed with some flint pebbles, otherwise it will melt together and yield no **spirits** <note>volatile vapors or liquids</note>. This is one of the best **Grading-Waters** for **silver** <note>original symbol: "☽"</note> and for **lead** <note>original symbol: "♄"</note>. One can

94. **Note well.** <note>original Latin: "NB"</note> All **tinctures**, **grading-oils** <term>oils used to improve the color or quality of metals, typically to give them the appearance of gold</term>, or **grading-waters**, which are made only from volatile **sulphur** <note>original: "Sulph."</note> and saline parts, do nothing or very little. 95. These things, although they are all described quite clearly, are nonetheless not for a beginner, but require a skilled **laborant** <term>an experienced practitioner of laboratory chemistry</term> who must be capable of deep reflection, because **fire** is the master in these matters—too much or too little brings harm. There must also be the knowledge to separate the **dregs** <note>original Latin: "Feces"</note> from the ascended tinctures, oils, and waters, and the lees from the salts, so that only the pure parts are taken; otherwise, it causes harm and prevents the **transmutation** <term>the alchemical transformation of one substance into another</term>. ...reduce the cement powder in this way: Unslaked lime, crushed small, salt <note>original symbol: 🜔</note>, potash, and shiny furnace-soot, equal parts of each <note>original Latin: "ana."</note>; these are boiled in urine until everything is dissolved. 96. A clever artist will wonder why I have not included cinnabar <note>mercury sulfide, typically used for its red pigment and mercury content</note> among the **species** <term>the specific ingredients or components of a mixture</term>, since it is included by almost all writers of books. I allow it for such coarse work and mixtures as they make; I, however, unlock the "bodies" <note>the physical forms of the metals</note> and release the volatile and fixed **sulphur** <note>original: "Sulph."; here referring to the combustible or "soul" principle of the metal</note> from their bonds so that they become spiritual <note>meaning they transition into a gaseous or essential state</note>, so that they may enter the waters and impart their **tinctures** <note>the concentrated essence or color-giving principle</note> into them. Now, if I were to use cinnabar, it would not be useful to me; it is nothing but **sulphur** and **mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note>. I already have enough sulfur present, and the mercury causes me harm because it seizes the golden **sulphur** more readily than the common kind, **precipitates** itself with it, and remains among the coarse **feces** <term>the dregs, waste, or impure sediment</term> and comes to naught. How then can the golden **sulphur** which the mercury has seized enter the grading-water-oils <term>specialized liquids used to "grade" or improve the color and quality of metals</term> or **tinctures** and become spiritual? I say that cinnabar ruins it and creates a useless expense, because it is costly.

97. However, to demonstrate a useful process for cinnabar <note>mercury sulfide</note> as well, one must make the cinnabar oneself. Melt 2 parts sulphur <note>original: Sulph.</note> so that it does not catch fire, and pour one part mercury <note>original symbol: ☿</note> into it. Stir this over the fire until it unites with the sulphur, becomes thick and tough like thick pitch, and no more mercury is visible. This is then sublimated <term>a process where a solid is heated into a vapor and then cooled back into a solid form, skipping the liquid phase</term> into cinnabar. Grind it small and pour oil of vitriol <note>original: Oleo 🜔; concentrated sulfuric acid</note> over it; digest it for several days. The oil of vitriol must be strong. When it is dry and the phlegm <term>the watery, tasteless part of a distilled substance</term> has smoked away, pour onto it the red oil of antimony <note>original symbol: ♁</note> which has been strengthened by a dissolved saffron of iron <note>original: Eisen Saffran; an iron oxide used for its coloring and chemical properties</note>, as described in No. 86. This will dissolve the cinnabar. It must be ground in the warmth, otherwise it becomes wet and muddy. Afterward, keep it in the fire until it has flowed into a **fixed stone**, which can then be alloyed with **gold** <note>original symbol: ☉</note> or **silver** <note>original symbol: ☽</note>; it will yield a good portion more than its own weight.

Pour off the water, melt **silver** <note>original symbol: ☽</note> or **gold** <note>original symbol: ☉; Sol</note>, and gradually add the boiled **mercury** to the molten metal. Continue boiling **mercury** in the salt-water until no more of it will harden <note>this refers to the mercury becoming "fixed" or stabilized</note>. If the "sweet water" boils away, one must replenish it with more to keep the solution thin; this prevents it from becoming too sharp <note>corrosive</note> and dissolving the **mercury** entirely. The salts can all be used again for a new process.

**Note Well.** In all <term>cementations</term> <note>a process where a metal is surrounded by powdered minerals and heated to alter its properties without melting it</note> with salt and <term>sulfur 🜍</term>, the fire must be gentle so that the material does not melt and only the <term>species</term> <note>the specific outward forms or chemical components</note> are corroded; otherwise, the heat will simply reduce the metallic bodies to their base state.

**Mercury Solution** <note>original: ☿. Solut.</note>; one must learn to recognize this sign. > Clothed in purple, and, as I have heard,
> He will reward your toil: Well for you, you have it good;
> Preserve this treasure as dearly as your own life and blood.
> Look! Thus is he blessed by God in this world,
> Who meets Him with pure love at all times;
> The pure Fear of God attains such a reward,
> The Fear of God alone crowns a son of virtue.

# Preface

<image-desc>Decorative typographic banner at the head of the page featuring a central crown symbol flanked by symmetrical rows of asterisks and cross-shaped fleurons within a rectangular double-line border.</image-desc>

In my previous little treatise—which is named *The Mineral Gluten*, *The Double Serpent-Staff* <note>original: "Schlangen-Stab"; a reference to the Caduceus of Hermes/Mercury</note>, *The Mercury of the Philosophers* <note>original: "Mercurius Philosophorum"</note>, and *The Long and Short Path to the Universal Tincture*—I promised to publish another little treatise concerning the power and effect of the Tincture <term>Tincture: in alchemy, a potent substance capable of transforming base metals into gold or healing the human body</term>, especially regarding its use in medicine. However, near the end of that little book, I used these formal terms: "Enough has been said concerning the growth of the 3 Principles, namely: 1. of the external world, 2. of the inner and Light-world, and 3. of the angelic and heavenly world." Yet, I did not carry this out according to these three worlds, nor did I explain myself at length regarding the **multiplication** <term>multiplication: the process by which an alchemist increases the quantity or the transformative power of the Philosopher's Stone</term>. Therefore, the reader might wonder and wish to know what was meant by it. Thus, I have for the time being set aside that promised little treatise, in order to first address the multiplication of this growth of the 3 Principles, according to all three worlds.

<s>)( 2</s> <meta>catchword: me</meta>

<summary>In this preface, the author explains the delay of a promised book on medical alchemy to first clarify the complex "multiplication" of alchemical principles across the physical, spiritual, and heavenly realms.</summary>
<keywords>Preface, Universal Tincture, Three Principles, Multiplication, Alchemical Medicine, Mercury of the Philosophers</keywords>

--- Page 116 ---
<meta>This page continues the author's preface, moving from the promise of explaining "multiplication" to defining the "3 Worlds" (Mineral, Vegetable, and Animal) as they apply to alchemical philosophy. It follows the catchword "me" from the previous page, completing the word "mich" (me/myself).</meta>

*) 0 (*

...wanting to explain myself better as to which 3 worlds I understand philosophically <note>original: "Philosophice"</note> in our work, because it possesses 3 kingdoms just as the great world <note>the macrocosm or the universe at large</note> does. 

As 1. The **mineral**: because it has its beginning and origin from this. 

2. The **vegetable**: because it grows, for all 7 metals <note>In alchemy, these are Gold, Silver, Mercury, Copper, Iron, Tin, and Lead</note> grow out of it, and from such grow the luminous planets as bright, sparkling stars, the very purest gemstones, and **Tinctures** <term>Tincture: a potent alchemical liquid used to transmute metals or restore health</term>. 

3. The **animal**: because it has nothing but living spirits, such as **Earth-spirits, Water-spirits, Air-spirits, and Fire-spirits** <note>These refer to elemental beings (Gnomes, Undines, Sylphs, and Salamanders) that the author believes inhabit the physical elements</note>. 

However, someone might say to me: why then did I call the heavens and Paradise a world? To this the answer serves: that between our heavenly and paradisiacal world, and the Divine Heaven and Paradise, there is a great difference, and ours is only a **mirror**, in which we behold the former; for we know well that God created not one throne for the holy angels, but many.

# Content of the First Treatise.

First Treatise concerning the Universal <note>original: "Universal." In alchemy, the "Universal" refers to the "Universal Medicine" or the "Philosopher's Stone," a substance believed to be able to perfect both metals and the human soul.</note> according to the growth of the three Principles, how it compares with all three worlds: the outer and dark world, the light and paradisiacal world, and the angelic <note>original: "Englischen." In this context, "Englisch" is the archaic German adjective for "Angel" (Engel), not the English language or nation.</note> and heavenly world. In this Universal, His entire creation across all three worlds is touched upon in summary. It is described beginning from its coarse, impure, and dark nature—what forms, smells, and tastes exist in the outer world—as well as all seven source-spirits <term>Source-spirits: *Quell-Geister*, a term popularized by the mystic Jacob Boehme, referring to the seven fundamental qualities or forces of nature (such as "harshness" or "bitterness") that drive both spiritual and material existence.</term> in their harsh, bitter, sour, and fierce quality contained within it. It describes how it must be separated from this "bad nature" and placed into the light, into the glowing, healthy water of life, where all seven source-spirits become pure, white, sweet, bright, and glowing, and finally all issue forth as one, becoming tangible and a perfect nature; this is called the building of Paradise. It also describes how this paradisiacal body is transferred into the angelic and heavenly world, where these seven forms of nature in the angelic world—through the pure fire-spirits, which are the seven source-spirits of the angelic world—transform these paradisiacal bodies into bright, shining stars and gemstones. Thus, our seven metals become the planetary stars that travel upon high axes and are transformed into pure heavenly spirits through the air and heavens of the angelic world, which is called the threefold magic wheel, and the thrice-seven

Our **metallic seed** is not far removed from us; otherwise, a human life would be too short to make a **tinging stone** <note>A substance capable of "tinging" or transforming base metals into gold or silver.</note> out of it that would be fixed and incombustible in the fire, because our **Matter** <term>original: *Materia*; the primary substance required to begin the alchemical Great Work</term> must be incombustible. Out of metals, through metals, and with metals the Stone is made; though the **Matter** is not strictly a metal, it is the **flower of metals**; nor is it strictly a mineral, yet it is most closely related to minerals. It is **vegetable** <note>In alchemy, "vegetable" refers to the power of growth and reproduction, not just plants.</note> because it grows and is endowed with a **living soul**, and the vegetable life-giving water is prepared from it; it can also be applied to all three kingdoms.

It is very useful to the **mineral kingdom**, because it transforms such bodies into **Gold** <term>Symbol: ☉; represents the Sun, perfection, and the soul</term> and **Silver** <term>Symbol: ☽; represents the Moon, purity, and the mind</term>. It is even more useful to the **vegetable kingdom**, so that all old trees become fertile through it, and one can perform many thousands of wonders in this kingdom with it, because all vegetable essences can be separated in a short time by this fire.

For the **animal kingdom**, it is most glorious. What surpasses health? This **balsam** heals from within and without. If God had not decreed death because of sin, humans would be immortal through it. These pure **elements** now seem indeed pure and separated, though it is impossible to separate them completely; the Earth still has sulfurous fatness; the **Mercury** <term>Symbol: ☿; representing the principle of fluidity and volatility</term> or Water has even more; the Air also has **Mercury** or Water with it; the Fire has much of the earthly, such as earth, all of which is to be seen in the **Composition** <note>The "Composition" is the stage where the purified elements are recombined to form the final Philosopher's Stone.</note>.

# Conclusion
## of this First Treatise.

In heaven is the <term>Sun of Righteousness<note>A title for Christ derived from Malachi 4:2, widely used in mystical and devotional literature to describe Him as the source of spiritual life.</note></term>, the Son of GOD, Christ Jesus, who illuminates all heavenly crowns, angels, and holy people; from Him they have their life, light, and power. Without this divine light, everything would be dark and dead, without light, love, and grace. In the <term>great world<gloss>The macrocosm or physical universe.</gloss></term> is the sun, which illuminates all stars and indeed the whole world, for it is the spirit of the entire world, from which it receives its power, light, life, growth, and fertility, as if from its life-giving spirit; for without the sun or its shine, everything would be dead, dark, and frozen. In our <term>small world<gloss>The microcosm, or the individual human being.</gloss></term> there is also our sun, which illuminates everything, makes it alive, and gives life and growth; without it, or its warmth, fire, and light, everything would be dead, without power, life, and <term>tincture<note>In the alchemical and mystical tradition of this period, a "tincture" refers to a vitalizing spiritual essence that gives color, quality, and life to matter.</note></term>. # Conclusion

In heaven, there is the Sun of Righteousness, the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who illuminates all heavenly crowns, angels, and holy people. It is from him that they derive their life, light, and power; without this divine light, everything would be dark and dead, devoid of light, love, and grace. But if the **old Adam** overcomes us—the sinful birth with which we stand in wrath and the Devil's kingdom—then we belong to that even after death. For here, throughout our entire life, we stand with one foot in the **paradisiacal world of light**, and with the other in the **dark world of wrath**, the kingdom of the Devil and of Hell. Now, when man triumphs and overcomes through **Christ**, he sees the danger in which he was stuck, and learns to guard himself against the Devil, and is entirely separated from him in death. # The Fourth Treatise.
## Concerning the Universal Stone, or Universal Tincture.

Whoever wishes to prepare this, let him seek the Light; this dwells within man, in the understanding, and also in all the creatures of God. Let man pray to God, and He will enlighten him through His divine light, and open his darkened understanding, so that he might first find the new man within the earth—that is, within himself—and in that same man find the Kingdom of God, the precious pearl. ## Our Matter.
<note>original: "Unsere Materia." The author is defining the "prima materia," the starting substance required for the alchemical process.</note>

This is but a single **Matter**, from which our beginning and end proceed. His voice like the roar of great waters, etc. Its **salt-water** is the roaring and raging sea; when it is to be united with its fixed part, storm-winds occur which move the sea too greatly.

## Interpretation of this third figure regarding the natural Great Work.

The book with seven seals is the **foliated earth** <term>geblätterte Erde: a layered or "leafy" mineral state reached during the alchemical process, representing a purified substrate</term>, which comes into birth from the preceding seven spirits and is sublimated from such crystal and glass-like **Azoth** <term>Azoth: the "universal medicine" or essential mercury of the philosophers, considered the beginning and end of the Work</term>. This is closed with seven seals and prepared through seven **imbibitions** <note>Eintränkungen: the process of repeatedly soaking a dry substance with liquid until it is saturated</note>, which are the seven forms of nature; here, however, they are our seven metals. These are brought to the highest degree through seven systems into the white **Sun** <note>original symbol: ☉, usually meaning gold, but here specified as "white"</note>, into the foliated earth or **fixed Moon** <term>Luna fixa: silver that has been rendered stable and resistant to the fire, a key stage in achieving the Great Work</term>, which appears beautiful, white, and yellow. Now, nothing can unlock this book, or break open and resolve its seven seals, unless it has sprung from this very blood, or partakes in it, having a dual nature: both spiritual and physical.

The seven horns indicate that the dissolving and restoring power also springs from these seven forms and from these degrees. The seven eyes represent his dual spiritual nature, along with the life-giving soul. This dual spirit can break through the seven seals. At the opening of each seal, a great change occurs in the work during its **exaltation** <term>Exaltation: an operation by which a substance is raised to a higher state of purity, color, or power</term>. Much could be written about this in a spiritual manner, and also regarding this physical work, but for now I strive for brevity, until finally the earthquake occurs at the six seals, when the sun becomes black and the moon is transformed into blood <note>A reference to the "nigredo" or blackening stage of alchemy, often described using apocalyptic imagery from the Book of Revelation</note>.

# Explanation of this fourth figure concerning
## The great natural work.

The Angel comes clothed with a cloud, a rainbow upon his head, his face like the sun, his feet like pillars of fire, etc. <note>A description of the angel in Revelation 10:1</note>. This is our **Virgin’s Son**, who has taken his birth through the **seven forms of nature** <term>Seven forms of nature: In the alchemical philosophy of Jakob Böhme and his followers, these are the seven foundational qualities—such as contraction, expansion, and rotation—that make up all created matter</term> and through the many colors of the rainbow. He consists of **water and earth**, upon which he sets both his feet; this indicates his double nature. He now ascends in a dry cloud as the **dry living water** <term>Dry water: An alchemical paradox describing a substance that flows like a liquid but does not wet the hands, representing a highly purified metallic essence</term>, because of his purity and heavenly nature in **soul, spirit, and body**. Our ore has been purified seven times through the white fire, so the fixed element—the earth—beholds his feet as pillars of fire, and his face shines like the sun, etc. 

He is entirely **golden** in his whole nature, which creates a **golden mirror**, a golden luster over the earth and the sea. This is the true life-giving spirit and consists of three parts: **soul, spirit, and body**. It possesses divine virtues and is the wonder of Nature and Art, the **fountain of living water** that wets no hand. 

The great voice, etc., is his praise and glory. When he roars in his strength like a **lion**, the **seven thunders** raise their voices, etc. <note>Revelation 10:3</note>. When he, through seven repeated **imbibitions** <term>Imbibitions: The alchemical process of repeatedly adding a liquid "nourishment" to a solid substance to mature or transform it</term>, leads his brothers, the phi-

## Spiritual Interpretation of this Fifth Figure.

The woman clothed with the sun, etc., is the Christian Church, the pure humanity of the new man in the life of **JESUS** Christ, clothed with the sun—with Christ, whom she received in baptism. She has under her feet the moon, etc., representing all things temporal and transitory, etc., and the many separations and source-spirits <term>Source-spirits: Translated from "Quel-Geister," a term central to the mysticism of Jakob Böhme. These are the seven foundational "qualities" or forces of nature that can produce either harmony or conflict within the soul.</term>, which she does not allow to rule over her, but instead treads underfoot. The crown of 12 stars, etc., refers to the holy teachers of the Apostles and Prophets. She has trodden under her feet all 7 forms of nature and of the creature; she has resisted the evil influence and provocation of the planets, as well as her own source-spirits and evil impulses, and has not allowed them to rule over her. She is pregnant with the new man in Christ and suffers great agony in childbirth before she can tear herself away from the world and her own desires, so that Christ may take shape within us <note>This refers to the "Christ-within" or the "New Birth," a core concept where the believer undergoes a spiritual transformation mirrored by the biblical birth of Christ.</note>; therefore, the Church, the bride of Christ—the inner man—must suffer and endure much. ## Interpretation of the Fifth Figure in the Great Natural Work.

# Preface.

Beloved and, according to the honors due your station, respected reader. Among all authors who have ever written of the secret <term>chemical science</term> <note>original: "Chymischen Wissenschafft"; in this context, the term refers to the art of alchemy and the transformation of matter</note>, none has—without wishing to boast—expressed themselves so clearly, plainly, and brightly, regarding both the preliminary and the final stages of the work, as I have in my two small treatises: the *Mineral Gluten* <note>original: "mineralischen Gluten"; "gluten" in alchemy often refers to a sticky, cohesive "first matter" or universal glue</note>, and the *Philosophical Pearl-Tree*, the *Growth of the 3 Principles* <note>original: "3. Principien"; likely referring to the Paracelsian triad of Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury</note>, and now here in this treatise. Within these pages, the secrets of this art are presented to the world entirely naked and revealed, which all other <term>philosophers</term> <note>original: "Philosophi"; historical alchemical masters were commonly called philosophers</note> have otherwise kept concealed. They have only occasionally let a word slip, as if murmuring in their sleep, taking pleasure in telling such sweet dreams to posterity, through which no one...

<summary>In this preface, the author claims to provide a uniquely clear and transparent explanation of alchemical secrets, contrasting his directness with the cryptic and "dream-like" writings of previous alchemical masters.</summary>

## First Question.
### What is the Treasury of Nature?

**Answer.** It is all of nature itself: Firstly, according to the fiery, dark world. Secondly, according to the watery **Elementary** world. Thirdly, according to the astral world of the air, within which are the stars and planets. Fourthly, according to our world, which is called the mortal, transient world, as it now stands in its divided state; for **GOD** has partitioned it into the four **Elements**, namely Air, Water, Fire, and Earth. Fire occupies the highest place, followed by Water; in the Air is the light of the stars, and these **Meteora** <term>Meteora</term> <note>In early modern science, "meteora" refers to all atmospheric and celestial phenomena, including weather and planetary influences, believed to affect the Earth.</note> act upon the Earth, which, like a **Magnet**, draws the influences from the Air to itself. However, to describe all of nature or all of its powers and effects is possible for no man; even if he lived a thousand years, he would still not explore or experience it all. ### XVII.

Many people say, however, that while some have created a **Tincture**—that is, the **Stone**—they were unable to achieve the **Multiplication** <note>The process of increasing the quantity or the transformative power of the Stone.</note>. Because of this, they ruined the entire Tincture once again; where previously it had <term>tinted</term> <note>The act of the Stone transforming a base metal into gold or silver.</note> 1,000 parts, afterward it did nothing or very little. **Answer:** I certainly believe this happens when they contaminate the purified, boiled-down Tincture with impure leaden and arsenical spirits. It is no different than if one crushed a **gemstone**, mixed it with coarse brick dust, and then melted them together; who could then retrieve this gemstone from such earth and filth? 

Or, when they attempt to unite it with the **vivifying spirit** <note>The life-giving essence or "soul" of the matter.</note>, they mix it incorrectly; where they should take the **red**, they take the **white**. Instead of the "dry water" which wets no hand and is called **ointment** or **oil**, they take raw and unripe wet <term>menstrua</term> <note>original: "Menstrua." Potent solvents used to dissolve solids in the alchemical process.</note>. By doing so, they extinguish the fire of the Tincture. They add the unripe, raw, and uncooked to that which is mature and boiled. Since such a fiery body requires **fire** for its food, they instead give it **Virgin’s Milk** <note>original: "Jungfer-Milch." A term for a specific white mercurial liquid or solvent used in the early stages of the work.</note>. This was only used previously for the raising of this "child" <note>The early stage of the Stone's development.</note>; but now, as a **strong man**, the Stone no longer needs such food.

### XVIII.
**If one must unlock so many doors before entering the Treasure Chamber of Nature, what then does one see in the first room?**

**Answer:** There is nothing beautiful to be seen inside; it is an old, leprous man in a bath, covered in scales, spots, and leprosy. He is being purified by the bath so that his scales and spots are cleansed away, and his body emerges pure and healthy. <note>In alchemical symbolism, the "leprous man" represents base metals or the "First Matter" which is "sick" (impure) and must be healed (purified) into gold.</note>

### XIX.
**Is this then the old man's internal purification, and with what kind of water is he bathed, and how long does he remain in the bath?**

**Answer:** This bath only washes the body clean on the outside; internally, this water does nothing. It does not have the power to separate the pure from the impure <note>original Latin: "purum ab impuro"</note>. It is the bath of Nature and her vinegar. As for the time, many superfluous things <note>original Latin: "superflua"</note> are often done here; it can certainly be accomplished in a few days, though many a man might toil for half a year with this <term>Solution</term> <note>The process of dissolving a solid substance into a liquid state, often the first major step in alchemy.</note>.

### XX.
**What is done next with this old man?**

**Answer:** One squeezes out his water-blisters and sores until his body becomes dry and blood-red. The stinking water that has steamed from him and smoked out of all his limbs—from his hands, feet, head, and hair—is taken after its <term>Rectification</term> <note>The process of refining a distilled liquid by distilling it again to increase its purity or potency.</note>, and he is bathed once more—

**XXI. Is this then the second key?**

**Answer:** It is indeed, and it arises from the first key, just as one must use it to unlock the second door. Thus it is found that this Old Man carries a small, beautiful, and pure child within his body. But he himself is **Vulcan** <note>The Roman god of fire, representing the transformative heat of the furnace.</note>, the snake or dragon, who releases nothing but fire and smoke from his mouth, nose, ears, hands, feet, and all his limbs.

**XXII. Is this then Jupiter <term>♃</term>?**

**Answer:** No, it is the stone which **Saturn** <term>♄</term> swallowed instead of his son **Jupiter** <term>♃</term>, and which he must vomit up again; that is, to lead the stone over into a volatile <note>To "lead over" into a volatile state means to cause a solid substance to vaporize or transform through heat.</note> state. If **Saturn** does not swallow such a stone and spit it out again, he is not fit for the Work.

**XXIII. Now when Saturn <term>♄</term> has eaten the Sun-stone <term>☉; gold</term> and spat it out again, what should be done thereafter?**

**Answer:** One should purify the four children or four **elements** <term>elements; the fundamental building blocks of nature: Earth, Air, Fire, and Water</term>. The fire is the **element of fire** <note>original: "Elementum ignis"</note>, coming from the red **Venus** <term>♀; copper</term>—not from the common one which is green <note>Common copper often has a green patina (verdigris), but the "philosophical" copper is refined to a red state.</note>—this is **Pluto**. **Neptune** is the god of the sea or water; **Jupiter** <term>♃</term> is the god in the air, the highest; and the earth is **Saturn** <term>♄</term>.

## XXIV. Is then the previous *Saturn* not the right *Saturn*, and is there yet another?

**Answer:** The previous **Saturn** <term>♄; lead</term> carries the true one within his body like a beautiful little child; and it is this which is the philosophical **Saturn**, who is revealed after the separation of the four **elements** <term>the fundamental building blocks of matter: Earth, Air, Fire, and Water</term>, arising from the **quintessence** <term>the "fifth essence" or purest soul of a substance</term> of those four elements. The previous **Saturn** <term>♄</term> was of the coarse earth, created by Nature and available to all **Artists** <note>In alchemical texts, "Artists" refers to practicing alchemists or "Sons of Art."</note>; however, the philosophical **Saturn** must be brought forth by the Sons of Art themselves. This one has its beginning from the **Spirit of Mercury** <term>☿; the volatile, life-giving principle in alchemy</term>, which rises out of the sea from **Neptune** <note>Neptune here symbolizes the "mercurial sea" or the watery source of the metallic seed.</note>. I have also stated long ago that all **metals** grow out of common elemental water and are the fruits of **meteors** <note>Alchemists often categorized metals as "meteors" or "mineral vapors" because they believed metals condensed from vapors within the Earth's crust.</note>; likewise, the philosophical metals grow from our **elemental** water. Just as many metals as grow through Nature, so many do we also have through Art—and Art can reach higher than Nature, which can go no further than the creation of metals and gemstones, for she possesses only the coarse **elements**. We, however, have **impregnated** <note>original: *imprægnirt*</note> the coarse elemental water with one of the most perfect **bodies**, which comes from the **prime entity** <note>original: *primo ente*; the fundamental, first-existing state of matter</note> of the **Sun** <term>☉; gold</term> and the **Moon** <term>☽; silver</term>, and indeed of all the planets. This we have purified for a first, second, and third time, and separated into the four elements. Now there remains only the separation of the **pure from the impure** <note>original: *purum ab impuro*</note>, which transcends the elements; from these refined elements we generate the metals—these seven metals—which grow therefrom and are far more magnificent bodies than the common ones. From such as these, we also make precious stones,

### XXV. But this description depicts a very tedious task, yet in other books one reads that the Stone is made in two nights and three days?

**Answer:** The reason that this **Stone** seems to be described here as such a tedious task is because no one in the world has described the **Pre-Work**. Instead, they have all begun by writing about the **Separation of the Elements** without giving the seeker any prior light on how the matter should be purified and made ready so that it *can* be separated into the elements—except for perhaps an occasional word that slipped out. Because I have seen that the matter is difficult enough as it is, and that not one person in a thousand is granted the ability to untie this **Gordian Knot** <term>an ancient metaphor for an extremely complex problem</term> <note>original: "Nodum Gordium"</note>, I have chosen out of compassion and mercy not to withhold this from my fellow man. ### XXVI. Are the previous ones then the right keys?

**Answer:** They are the right keys, but they have only opened outer nature, followed by the gates and elements; in the future, however, the secret keys to the cabinet and secret treasury of nature will follow.

### XXVII. What then are the secret keys called and how many are there?

**Answer:** There are three of them. The first is called **Dissolution** <note>original: *Solutio*</note>. The second, **Joining** <note>original: *Conjunctio*</note>. The third is called **Fixing** <note>original: *Fixatio*</note>. The first opens the inner chamber of the Earth and is again divided into as many keys as **Dissolution**, **Hardening** <term>Coagulatio; the thickening of a liquid into a solid</term>, **Sublimation** <term>Sublimatio; the process of vaporizing a substance to purify it</term>, **Distillation** <term>Distillatio</term>, **Joining**, and when the Soul is drawn out from the Body <note>original: *Corpus*</note> by the Spirit and separated from the Soul and Spirit in the dissolution; therefore it is also called **Separation** <note>original: *Separatio*</note> and **Decay** <term>Putrefactio; the symbolic rotting of the matter to release its essence</term>. The second key, **Joining**, brings the tinging <note>In alchemy, a "tincture" or "tinging" power is the ability of the Stone to transform the color and nature of base metals.</note> and coloring Spirit into the new **Body**. The third, **Fixing**, shapes everything into everlasting stability.

XXX. But when **Mercury (☿)** is spoken of, what is it actually?
**Answer:** Firstly, when **Mercury (☿)** is spoken of, it is not common quicksilver, but our **raw spirit**. In the second way, it is our **calcining water**, which dissolves all bodies. Thirdly, it is the **Mercury (☿)** of the body which it has dissolved—the body of the **white Sulphur (🜍)**. The fourth is the **Mercury (☿)** or the **natural Sulphur (🜍)**.

Regarding its **congelation** <note>Solidification or "freezing" of a liquid substance.</note>: one must congeal the Mercury with the **Body of Magnesia** <note>original: *Cörper Magnesiæ*; here Magnesia refers to the raw mineral matter of the Stone.</note>. This is not the common quicksilver, nor the Magnesia one sees with the eyes; rather, by "Mercury" is understood the fruits of this mixture, which is the **radical moisture** <note>original: *humidum radicale*; the innate, life-giving moisture believed to reside in all matter.</note>.

The Mercury is a **Spirit**, and is called the "permanent water," or the **Vinegar**, the **Menstruum** <note>A solvent used to dissolve solids.</note>, or the **Nutriment** <note>original: *Nutrimentum*; food/nourishment</note> of Sulphur. It comes out of the Body and is of a white color. This **Sulphur** must be composed or prepared, and what comes from it is the **Mercury of the Philosophers** <note>original: *☿ philosophorum*</note>, which has been transformed into a white, dry Body.

From this comes thereafter the Divine or Heavenly state. And it is the same with the **Red Oil of the Philosophers** <note>original: *rothen Oleo Philosophorum*</note>, or its liquor. As for the **Incombustible Oil**, this is understood to be the oil of the **Ferments** <note>original: *Fermenten* or *Höfel* (yeasts); substances used to "leaven" or trigger transformation in the alchemical matter.</note>, before they are Sulphur, or when they are Sulphur—referring to their oils or solutions. The **Red Mercury**, or the Fire of the Stone, Soul and Oil, Red Tincture—these are all one and the same.

The **White Mercury** is the Air and Water of the Stone. The Oil—its Fire and Soul—remains behind at the bottom of the vessel. The Earth, when it is black, is called "the Earth"; after its **calcination** <note>The process of reducing a substance to ash through heat.</note>, it is white as snow, and its salt is [extracted]...

**XL. What then is this called, when it has been fixed <note>To "fix" a substance in alchemy means to make a volatile or evaporating spirit stable under the heat of fire</note>, or calcined <note>Reduced to a powder through high heat</note>?**

**Answer.** It is called the **glassy sea**, which can be mixed with fire; the natural treasure; the stone of the first order; and the **first tincture on white** <note>The *Albedo* or white stage of the alchemical process</note>. It appears somewhat greenish; its taste is harsh, which however afterwards turns into a sweetness.

**XLI. What then is the red tincture called?**

**Answer.** It is called the first tincture on red, the first stone on red, the bloody stone.

**XLII. What then is the Red Man?**

**Answer.** It is the red oil, the element of fire, from the philosophical **Sun** <term>Sun <note>Symbol: ☉; represents Gold or the perfected masculine principle</note></term>. The coral-red juice.

**XLIII. What then is the White Woman?**

**Answer.** The white **Venus** <term>Venus <note>Symbol: ♀; here representing the feminine principle or refined copper</note></term> of Nature, which is now dried out; the white moonlight.

**XLIV. What then is the Green Lion <term>Lion <note>Symbol: ♌</note></term>?**

**Answer.** It is the innermost **Sun** <term>Sun <note>Symbol: ☉</note></term>, the Sun's fixed salt, which is called the **little Green Lion** <term>Lion <note>Symbol: ♌</note></term>, in whose belly’s innermost entrails the red stars have their seat. It is also the first white tincture, which one calls the natural treasure, and is made from this double salt. Also, this is called the **Green Lion**, the first oil of **Venus** <term>Venus <note>Symbol: ♀</note></term> from **Saturn** <term>Saturn <note>Symbol: ♄; often representing lead or the initial state of matter</note></term>, of the same kind and nature as Venus, called the **circling green moth** <note>original Latin: "tinea viridis girat"; likely a poetic or cryptic description of a chemical reaction involving a green residue or vapor</note>, through which **Mercury** <term>Mercury <note>Symbol: ☿; Quicksilver</note></term> is precipitated. These are green in their interior, and also reach the white tincture; for through the oil of **Saturn** <term>Saturn <note>Symbol: ♄</note></term>, the **Mercury** <term>Mercury <note>Symbol: ☿</note></term> is made fixed and transformed into the **glassy sea**.

**XLV. What then are the green and red Lions <term>Lions <note>Symbol: ♌; in alchemy, the Lion often represents a powerful solvent or the raw state of a metal capable of being "ennobled"</note></term> that enter into a bond of friendship with each other, other than the starry Lion with the Crown?**

**Answer.** It is the white tincture <note>The *Albedo* or white stage, capable of transmuting metals into silver</note>, which is united with the red Lion so that from the mouths of both the golden juice flows out; the white tincture becomes the red, and the green Lion—as the rising Sun <term>Sun <note>Symbol: ☉</note></term> or the Sun still hidden behind the Moon—is transformed into the red Sun, into the red tincture. Thus, the white tincture is given the name of the starry green Lion to distinguish it from the previous salt or green Lion, which is also called "visible gold" <note>Original: *aurum perspectibile*</note>.

**XLVI. What then are the Sun and the Moon?**

**Answer.** This is understood in many ways. Firstly, there is our moist Moon, which we also call **Virgin's Milk** <note>Original: *Jungfer-Milch*; a symbolic term for a white liquid or the refined essence of the matter</note>, which is hidden in our red earth; also, our white fire <term>Fire <note>Symbol: Δ</note></term> is called the Moon. Likewise, the white tincture is called this. Furthermore, our Sun <term>Sun <note>Symbol: ☉</note></term> is what we call the blood of the Sun <note>The essence of gold</note> before it is extracted from the red earth, and afterwards, when it has become the red, transparent Sun. This is also our Sun: the "foliated earth" <note>Original: *geblätterte Erde*; a flaky, purified state of the matter often compared to mica or crystals</note>, as well as the red fixed fire and the red tincture. But the true Sun is the compounded and fixed material of the Stone <note>The Philosopher's Stone</note> when Mercury <term>Mercury <note>Symbol: ☿</note></term> transforms into our rising Sun, and subsequently when such a Sun is colored yellow and red.

**XLVII. What then is the crowned Queen?**

**Answer.** It is the white tincture.

**XLVIII. What then is the crowned king?**
**Answer.** The red tincture <note>The final stage of the alchemical process (*Rubedo*), a substance capable of transmuting base metals into gold and acting as a universal medicine</note>.

**XLIX. What then is the Virgin's Milk?**
**Answer.** It is the Pontic water <note>A term for a specialized alchemical solvent, often considered "mercurial" and "acidic"</note>, the simple **Mercury** <term>Mercury <note>Symbol: ☿</note></term>, and the *circulatum minus* <note>Original Latin: "lesser circulation"; a lower-level distillation process</note>, when it is sublimated with its salt.

**L. What then is the Eagle?**
**Answer.** It is the **Mercury** of the Philosophers <note>Symbol: ☿; not common quicksilver, but the "living" essence sought by alchemists</note>.

**LI. What then is the foliated earth?**
**Answer.** It is the **Mercury**, which has been released from its watery moisture and has stepped out of the sea onto dry land <note>This describes a state where the matter has been dried or fixed, losing its liquid form</note>.

**LII. What then is the starry eagle?**
**Answer.** This is the same double **Mercury**, which is dissolved in its oil and called the *Great Circulate* <note>The final or "great" stage of the circulation/distillation process</note>, in spirit and body; it is the water that does not wet the hands, in which the king and queen bathe <note>A famous alchemical paradox describing a solvent that behaves like water but is actually a dry, metallic spirit</note>.

**LIII. What then is the Cyllenius <note>A classical epithet for the god Mercury, referring to his birth on Mount Cyllene</note> with outspread wings, whose two sides encompass the Sun and Moon?**
**Answer.** This very same multiplying and increasing menstruum <term>menstruum <note>From the Latin *menstruus*; in alchemy, this refers to a solvent that dissolves solids and extracts their essence</note></term>, the vegetable *aqua vitae* <note>Original Latin: "water of life"; here referring to a potent alchemical spirit</note>, in which the powers of the **Sun** <term>Sun <note>Symbol: ☉; Gold</note></term> and the **Moon** <term>Moon <note>Symbol: ☽; Silver</note></term> reside.

**LIV. What then is the Spirit of Mercury <note>Symbol: ☿</note>?**
**Answer.** It is the raw, unripe, and untimely mineral spirit, which is nonetheless an everlasting menstruum [solvent], for it dissolves all its parts one after another, all of which must also be taken from it until they are all refined and purified through it.

Nevertheless, he can elevate, illuminate, and color this precipitate in his own ferments, unguents, and salves as high as he wishes. LXXIV. <term>Roger Bacon<note>A 13th-century English philosopher and friar, often legendary in alchemy for his supposed discovery of the Elixir of Life</note></term>, an Englishman, has written: If you will restore the equal weight of the elements, then you will

One may then dissolve this precipitate again in its own tinting oils and poisons, make it fixed once more, and repeat this as often as one wishes, whereby the Tinctures are heightened more and more, and are able to transform far more parts than before. No man has yet described this as clearly as I am now doing; whoever understands and finds it will learn to recognize what gratitude he owes me.

# The Second Figure or Symbol.
## The Philosophical Stone composed of Spirit, Soul, and Body.

**Text and Verse:** Just as the snake here has three necks, and yet only one body, in which it keeps a cruel poison hidden: so also the **Multiplication** <note>original: "Fortpflanzung"; the process of increasing the power or quantity of the alchemical agent.</note> has three natures—of the **Sun** and the **Moon**—and holds a cruel poison in its body; therefore the **Raven**, **Peacock**, **Swan**, and **King** provide the colors, of which you may be certain once you see them with your own eyes.

## Interpretation.

The snake is the single <term>Matter</term> <note>original: "Materia"; the raw substance used at the start of the "Great Work."</note>, which initially, in its raw state, contains the three <term>Principles</term> <note>original: "Principia"</note> of **Salt** (🜔), **Sulfur** (🜍), and **Mercury** (☿) within itself and is poisonous; but during the work, when these three are separated from it, purified, and joined together again in the process of **Multiplication** and **Generation**—where **Sun** <note>Gold or the masculine principle.</note> and **Moon** <note>Silver or the feminine principle.</note> are begotten—it becomes even more poisonous. At first, it turns **black** <note>The *Nigredo* stage, representing putrefaction or death.</note>, thereafter iridescent with many colors <note>The *Cauda Pavonis* or Peacock’s Tail stage.</note>, and finally **white**—the "King in his Shirt" <note>A metaphor for the *Albedo* or white stage, where the matter is purified but not yet "clothed" in the final red color.</note> and the **Stone** in Soul, Spirit, and Body. When these are seen, one is assured that the **White Sulfur** (🜍) or the **White Tincture** <note>A liquid or powder capable of transforming metals; the white version transmuting them into silver.</note> can be obtained.

## The 2. Figure or Symbol.
### The Philosopher's Stone from Spirit, Soul, and Body.

**Text and Verse:** Just as here the serpent has three necks, and yet only one body, in which it keeps cruel poison hidden: So also the propagation <note>The process of "multiplying" or generating the Stone.</note> has three natures, those of the Sun and the Moon, and has cruel poison in its body; therefore the Raven, Peacock, Swan, and King also yield the colors, of which you can be certain when you see them with your eyes.

->Interpretation.<-

The serpent is the unique **Matter** <note>original: "Materia"; the "Prime Matter" or starting material of the Great Work.</note>, which initially in its rawness holds within itself the three **Principles** <note>original: "Principia"; the three fundamental components of all matter in alchemical theory.</note> **Salt** (🜔), **Sulfur** (🜍), and **Mercury** (☿), and is poisonous; but in the work, when these three are separated from it, purified, and put back together—in the propagation and generation where Sun and Moon <note>Sun and Moon here represent the metallic principles of Gold and Silver, or the masculine and feminine energies.</note> are begotten—it becomes even more poisonous, and first black <note>The "Nigredo" or "Raven" stage of decomposition.</note>, then variegated with many colors <note>The "Cauda Pavonis" or "Peacock’s Tail" stage.</note>, finally white <note>The "Albedo" or "Swan" stage.</note>, the King in his shirt <note>A metaphor for the Stone reaching the white, purified state before it is "clothed" in red.</note>, and the Stone in Soul, Spirit, and Body; when these are seen, one is assured that the white **Sulfur** (🜍), the white **Tincture** <note>original: "Tinctur"; the transformative substance capable of transmuting metals.</note> can be obtained.

If you want to know from where Delius <note>An epithet for Apollo, the sun god, who slew the Python.</note> takes the bow and arrows? Our reclining **Lion** (♌) shall tell you this.

## Interpretation.

The hard, fierce Python, grown thus from **Mercury** (☿) and Salt—from the earth, from water and salt—which is full of shining scales; this terrifying beast, which in its earthly caves dried up pure poison, and is now the white **Sulfur** (🜍) and **Mercury** (☿) of **Mercury**; this is the dragon that must be killed. It belongs to the "Old One" <note>likely referring to Saturn or the primordial matter</note>, having its beginning from **Saturn** (♄) of the Earth. Delius, with his warm arrows, slays it; this is the Oil of Saturn <note>original: "Oleum ♄"</note>. The reclining **Lion** (♌) is the fixed Earth, the Green **Lion** (♌).

# The 4. Figure or Symbol.

## Calcination, the 1. Degree of the Philosophers.

**Text and Verse:** Here at the table sits Cyllenius <note>An epithet for Mercury (Hermes), the messenger of the gods, often associated with the volatile principle.</note> with spread wings, whose two sides enclose the Sun and the Moon. Upon the table grow the herbs and flowers placed there, and the **Lion** (♌) devours the serpent, the **Mercury** (☿). Behold, the light spirit is fixed <note>term: "fixed" — to make a volatile substance stable and resistant to heat.</note> by the lime <note>original: "Kalck"; the powder or ash resulting from the process of calcination.</note>; therefore, it rejoices when it is united with the earth through its own sprouting and the greening of the flowers.

## Interpretation.

Cyllenius <note>An epithet for Mercury (Hermes), the messenger of the gods.</note>, who is enclosed on both sides by the Sun (☉) and the Moon (☽), is our **living water**. This water consists of soul, spirit, and body; within it, the Sun and Moon have their powers resolved <note>term: "resolved" — dissolved or broken down into their fundamental components.</note>. In this water, the most magnificent herbs—the **tinctures**—grow. Here, **Mercury** (☿) devours the serpent, which is also **Mercury** (☿), turning it into lime <note>original: "Kalck"; the powdered residue of calcination.</note> and calcining it. One must not rely upon the *sublimated* <note>The substance turned into vapor and resolidified.</note>, but rather upon the *calcined* substance. Now, this lime must be moistened with the **growing menstruum** <note>original: "Menstruo"; a powerful alchemical solvent.</note> so that it may sprout and turn green from its own earth. In this way, one nature rejoices in the other nature, and this light spirit is **fixed** <note>Made stable and resistant to heat.</note> by the lime; thus, our greening and growing ore becomes our **Sun** (☉).

Now, dissolve the **Magisterium** <note>The "Mastery" or the alchemical medicine in its current state of development.</note> which was prepared by the aforementioned lime, so that the **Mercury** (☿) may rise up through pleasant signs.

## Interpretation.

The **Lion** (♌) heated by the air or heaven is the **Solar Mercury** <note>original: "☿ Solaris"</note> extracted by the air or the heavenly **menstruum**, which the heaven

# The 6. Figure or Symbol.
## The Third Degree: Separation. <note>original: "Separatio."</note>

**Text and Verse:** The dissolved bonds shall fall away; the light shall rise into the heights, but the heavy shall sink down, so that each may be in its own place. From this comes the heaviness of the Earth, which shall cast down the light from the heights and, through a contrary degree, humble the proud hearts. Only the lightness of the Air, mixed with the dissolved heaviness, shall be able to adorn the same through its rays.

# Interpretation.

In all solutions <note>the process of dissolving solids into liquid</note>, separations occur. For philosophical separations are not violent like the common ones <note>likely referring to common mineral acids like aqua fortis</note>, which devour everything—pure and impure—without distinction. But in this solution, both separation and **conjunction** <note><term>Conjunction</term>: The alchemical "marriage" or reuniting of separated elements into a new whole.</note> take place, for the light spirits descend again and bring the body and soul with them

## The 7th Figure.
### The 4th Degree: Conjunction. <note>original: "Conjunctio"; the stage where separated elements are reunited into a new, stable form.</note>

Just as the desired Sun rises after sorrowful clouds, so too does greater love rise after anger. The bodies, which you have separated from one another, bring now together again, so that the seed may gladden you with many children. In the meantime, Neptune <note>original: "Neptunus"; in alchemy, Neptune often personifies the water bath or the solvent used to facilitate the chemical union.</note> can prepare a lukewarm bath so that husband and wife <note>likely referring to the union of the alchemical "Sulfur" and "Mercury."</note> may bathe themselves.

## Interpretation.

When the Sun has endured its darkness, after the sorrowful, murky clouds—for here no such blackness <note>A reference to the "nigredo," the stage of complete decomposition.</note> is to be seen in the multiplication, or rather in the composition; instead, it only becomes somewhat dark in color, very slightly blackish, dark, sky-blue, violet-blue, or reddish, until bright colors appear again and it is multiplied in its power. If it is to be further multiplied and exalted <note>refined or made more potent</note>, the baths must be heated and prepared anew.

Through this fixed body it is preserved again, as this spirit takes on a body in which it can rest; otherwise, it would be irretrievably lost and would have to vanish back into its *chaos* <note>the state of unorganized, raw matter from which the work began</note>.

# The 17th Figure.
## The Married State.

In our heaven, two lights shine simultaneously, which bring back the great lights of heaven. Join these two together, just as the woman is given together with the man, so that a lawful marriage-bed may come of it; therefore the transformation of the elements must also become rhythmic <note>original: "metrisch"; implying a balanced proportion or harmonious cycle</note>, so that the round form may bring forth its powers.

## Interpretation.

The two lights of heaven are our Sun and Moon; the Moon is our fixed white <term>Fire ($\triangle$)</term>, the Sun our red <note>In the original manuscript, a space was left here, likely for the symbol of the Sun (☉) or Gold</note>. These two are married as Man and Woman, so that the elements are transformed—the man into the woman, and the woman into the man. The <term>Mercury (☿)</term> <note>the liquid principle or "Quicksilver"</note>, <term>Jupiter (♃)</term> <note>the metal Tin</note>, and the <term>Fire ($\triangle$)</term> and <term>Mercury (☿)</term>; when fire is cooked in water, the entire nature of the water is transformed into fire. This could not happen sooner until the water was dried out and transformed into earth, and the earth into air; then the fire could burn in the air and water, because it could no longer be extinguished by the moisture of the water.

# The 19th Figure.
## Tincture.

The cruel beast pursues the tender maiden through pathless fields, and gnashes with a terrifying sound; <term>Mercury (☿)</term> cries out: "Hurry here, you beautiful nymph, with swift feet, and fear not the cruel danger of your grave. He who dies with me shall also, after sorrowful misfortune, rise joyfully to the desired goods."

## Interpretation.

The cruel beast is the dragon, which is also called the <term>Bond of Hell</term> <note>original: "Höllen-Band"; a common alchemical term for the crude, unrefined matter that "binds" the spiritual essence</note>. The tender maiden is the <term>foliated earth</term> <note>original: "geblätterte Erde"; referring to the flaky or layered structure of the mineral matter during purification</note>; because it is of a double nature—both masculine and feminine—it is sometimes taken for the man and sometimes for the woman. The <term>Mercury (☿)</term> who cries out after her is the <term>Menstruum</term> <note>An alchemical solvent capable of dissolving solids without destroying their "seed" or essential nature</note>, which is prepared from <term>Mercury (☿)</term> and consists of soul, spirit, and body; this is our <term>living water</term>. In this same water, the white fixed <term>Earth (♁)</term> <note>The symbol ♁ usually represents Antimony or the Earth; here it refers to the solid, purified state of the matter</note>—the white Tincture—must sink, melt away, and be reborn within it, to multiply and rise toward the goods of wealth. Here, the method is shown to fix, augment, and multiply the white Tincture, the <term>White Stone of the First Order</term>, into which no common fire enters, but rather the wise spirits.

# The 21st Figure.

## Two Kinds of Sulfur.

Behold, here come two lions with their necks joined together, entering into a strong bond of friendship with one another. You who seek the ferment <note>A substance added to the alchemical "work" to trigger a transformation or to "multiply" the power of the medicine</note>, join the two <term>sulfurs</term> <note>Original symbol: 🜍.
