# Interpretation.

The two lions here are the two sulfurs, the Red and the White, which must be brought together into one <term>sulfur</term> <note>🜍</note>. This cannot happen until the matter is dry and fixed; otherwise, the Red sulfur has no ingress <note>The ability of an alchemical substance to penetrate and transform the "body" of another</note> into it and will always float on top. But through the right means—the <term>medium of joining</term> <note>Latin: *medium conjungendi*; a third substance that acts as a bridge to unite two opposing or incompatible materials</note>—they pass into one another. The Fixed holds the Volatile, and they become one.

## The 24th Figure.
->Augmentation<- <note>original: "Augmentatio." This stage involves increasing the potency and quantity of the alchemical stone</note>

The first transforms it into the **White Tincture**, the other makes it red into the **Red Tincture**, the Red Glass. These three stones are all for the medicine and can be increased. The swift wings of the **Mercury** are the two increasing and multiplying **Menstrua** <note>original: "Menstrua." Here the weight is also indicated to some extent: the fixed part must be three or four times heavier than the volatile part, otherwise it could not **coagulate** <note>turn from liquid to solid</note> it and make it fixed.

# The 46th Figure.

## The Revival of the King. <note>original Latin: *Resuscitatio Regis*</note>

Now the highest power is given to our King, and he carries such great gifts from the paternal present. Although he overcomes all things, he is nonetheless overcome by a servant: This one dissolves the former's limbs through his sprouting forth; however, in such a way that the mother gathers the dissolved limbs, whereby both the mother and the servant receive great honor from it.

## Interpretation.

Our multiplied red <term>Tincture</term> <note>a potent substance capable of transforming base metals into gold or healing the body</note> as the Son of the Sun, now has the greatest power in the metallic kingdom and can place golden crowns upon everyone. However, if he wishes to multiply himself further, he must allow himself to be killed by a servant. Because no one is equal to him, his previous oils and spirits are very lowly compared to his current highness and nobility; yet because they sprouted from his former blood—from his grandparents, who were but poor peasants and subjects—they dissolve his limbs. But because the King is of such great virtue and remains in his former bath of blood and sweat, the lowly blood is improved by the Royal blood. The fixed <term>Jupiter</term> <note>symbolized by ♃; in this context, it likely refers to a stabilized metallic state, often tin or a specific stage of the work</note> sustains the volatile [spirit], and the volatile <term>dissolves</term> <note>original: *solvirt*</note> it. Through this struggle, the King once again becomes high and glorious; he expands his power and dominion, his land—the Earth—is increased, and he <term>tinges</term> <note>original: *tingiret*; the act of chemically and spiritually coloring or transforming a substance</note> even much further than before.

## The 47th Figure.
### Three Fountains of Everlasting Water. <note>original Latin: *Tres Fontes perennis Aquæ*</note>

We 3 watery fountains are seen in a cave of a hidden heavenly rock, and are adorned with heavenly waters. # Interpretation.

The Old Man is our **Saturn** <term>Saturn</term> <note>symbolized by ♄; in alchemy, Saturn represents lead, the heaviest and "darkest" stage of matter, associated with the beginning of the Work and the process of "death" or putrefaction</note>, who must be separated into Soul, Spirit, and Body; for the spirit and soul must leave the body, otherwise it cannot die. The spirit and soul may rest within it for a time, but not with permanence. However, when the body putrefies and is once again illuminated and enlivened by the spirit and soul after its glorified resurrection, then it is **Apollo** <term>Apollo</term> <note>the Greek sun god; used here to represent the "Kingly Body" or the perfected, incorruptible gold that results from the alchemical process</note>, our Kingly Body, which is no longer subject to **decay** <note>original: *Corruption*</note>, but rather they [the soul and spirit] dwell therein with permanence from then on. This is the new birth.

# The 52nd Figure.

->The Conjunction <note>original: *Conjunctio*; the union of opposites, such as male and female or Sun and Moon</note><-

Sun and Moon carry the most beautiful lilies in their hands, and in the center of the place, our **Apollo** is seen; therefore, they both unite their own powers, and thus he carries the Kingly Scepter with a strong hand; his brilliance is praised throughout the entire world, and his honor and praise flow into the wandering pack <note>original: *herumschweiffende Rotte*; this likely refers to the volatile elements or unrefined substances that are brought into order by the power of the King</note>.

# Interpretation.

The beautiful flowers or lilies, which Sun and Moon carry, are the two **Sulphurs** <term>Sulphurs</term> <note>symbolized by 🜍; the active, masculine principles of matter. Alchemists sought a "white sulphur" for making silver and a "red sulphur" for making gold</note>, the red and the white; from these, the **Tincture** <term>Tincture</term> <note>the legendary "Philosopher's Stone" in liquid form, capable of "dyeing" or transforming base metals into gold</note> grows greatly when they unite their powers. From this, afterwards, comes the great and powerful King, who rules in the entire metallic and mineral kingdom: the Son of the Sun.

## The 53rd Figure.

->Mortification <note>original: *Mortificatio*; the alchemical stage of "death" or "killing" the metallic base to release its essence</note><-

Now Honor becomes envious of our shining King, and ten youths from the common rabble kill him; everything becomes confused, and the Sun and Moon give many signs of their sadness through the darkness that has arisen during the day. A rainbow painted with many colors appears, which brings to the people the pleasant news of peace.

## Interpretation.

The King, who is thus killed, is the red **Fire** <term>Fire</term> <note>represented by the symbol Δ; in this context, it refers to the active "sulfuric" principle or the Tincture itself</note>. The Tincture is dissolved <note>original: *resolvirt*</note> back into its previous waters; therein the Sun and Moon rot when they are eclipsed in the **Dragon’s Head** <term>Dragon’s Head</term> <note>original: *Drachen-Haupt*; an astronomical point where the moon's path crosses the sun's, here symbolizing a state of "blackness" or eclipse in the matter</note>. Finally, the sign of grace—the rainbow with many colors—appears when the struggle has subsided and the heaven of the **Holy [Work]** <note>original: *h.*; likely an abbreviation for *Heiligen* (Holy) or *Hermetis* (Hermetic)</note> has run its course; thus the Tincture is multiplied. The 10 youths are 10 parts of the **Solvent** <term>Solvent</term> <note>original: *Menstrui*; a substance used to dissolve the solid matter to facilitate its transformation</note>.

## The 54th Figure.

->Putrefaction <note>original: *Putrefactio*; the stage of rotting or decay, essential for the separation of the soul from the "dead" body of the metal</note><-

The city is devastated by countless enemies and fire; therefore, the mad rabble also perishes with its King. The black ravens consume the fallen bodies; however, the spiritual part remains unharmed. When this spirit is once again united with the strong body—with the King—a source of new life shall arise for all.

# The 59th Figure.
## The New Motto or Token.

I am a beautiful goddess, sprouted from the very depths of the sea, which looks upon the whole earth through its course and flows around it; our breasts pour forth two little streams, namely of blood and of milk, which you may well know; when these two are mixed, leave them to gentle **Vulcan** <note>original: "Vulcano"; the Roman god of fire, representing alchemical heat</note> to prepare, and then the Moon and **Apollo** <note>The sun god, representing Gold or the "Rubedo" (red) stage of the work</note> will come to fulfill your wish.

# The 71st Figure.
## Matter of the Philosophers' Stone.

It is indeed only one thing, but there are also two of them, yes even three; whoever is wise will surely learn that I have not told him this merely to pass the time. For there is only one Dragon <note>The Dragon is a central alchemical symbol representing the "Prima Materia" or the raw, chaotic substance that must be tamed and transformed.</note>, of little value and old in years, which possesses the King’s Well and true recompense. There are two Mercuries <term>☿</term>, of which you must unite the constant or fixed one with the flying <note>In alchemy, "flying" refers to volatile substances that evaporate, while "fixed" refers to those that remain stable under heat.</note> one. It is a soul, a body, and a light spirit.

# Interpretation.

Our Matter <term>Materia</term> is but a single matter, within which is our beginning and end. There are also two of them, namely Male and Female, the active <term>agens</term> and the passive <term>patiens</term>; there are also three of them, the three Principles <term>Principia</term>: Salt <term>🜔</term>, Sulphur <term>🜂</term>, and Mercury <term>☿</term>. And yet it is only a single Dragon, the old, poisonous and smoking Saturn <term>♄</term> <note>Saturn, associated with lead, represents the heavy, "dead" state of matter before it is spiritualized.</note>; he holds the King's Well—the rich treasure—in his keeping. There are two Mercuries <term>☿</term>, the fixed and the flying; Brother and Sister, both of whom must become one body. There is a soul—the red blood; a body—the double Mercury; and a light spirit—called the Oil or Air-Spirit <term>Spiritus</term> <term>☿</term>. Thus far the figures, emblems, texts, and sayings of Master Stolcius <term>M. Stolceens</term> <note>Michael Stolcius von Stolzenberg was the author of the *Viridarium Chymicum* (1624), a famous collection of alchemical emblems which this text is interpreting.</note> have been interpreted. **LXXIX.** All these texts are difficult and obscure, as is their interpretation; can they not be given more easily?
**Answer.** They are neither difficult nor obscure, but rather everything is clear and easy; it is only hidden from those to whom GOD does not wish to give it, who are not meant to have it, and who would also use it poorly. For GOD looks upon the heart; He searches the heart and the kidneys <note>A biblical idiom meaning God examines one's deepest thoughts and emotions.</note>. That it could be described more clearly is not possible, for these things are not found on earth, but are shown through the <term>Sons of Art</term> <note>A traditional term for alchemists who have mastered the "Great Work."</note>. These have no names, no parents; they are new births and forms of nature, arising from the first, second, and third purification, and from so many compositions <note>original: "Compositionibus"</note>. From one come the elements <note>original: "Elementa"</note>; these reveal the three principles <note>original: "Principia"</note> <note>The three principles are Salt, Sulphur, and Mercury.</note>; the three principles reveal the metals; these are transformed into brightly shining stars, and into so many kinds of tinctures <note>original: "Tincturen"</note>. For this, one must have many kinds of solvents <note>original: "Menstrua"</note> <note>In alchemy, a "menstruum" is a solvent or catalyst used to dissolve solids.</note>, sometimes wet, sometimes dry spirits, as well as salt, water, oil, and fire. Now, what are all of these called, and how should one name them? And yet all of these come from a single thing. It reminds me of a man who is to beget many children with his wife; the children are now in his loins, but who sees them, or who can count how many there shall be, or what they shall look like? They likely all look like humans, but no two faces are like the other; one resembles the father, the other the mother; one is more masculine, the other more feminine

...nature, for they come from one father and one mother. Thus here also in our Work: where Saturn (♄), Jupiter (♃), and Mercury (☿) have the upper hand, they beget a feminine body, which is called Luna <note>The Moon, representing the silver or "white" stage of the work.</note>; but when Mars (♂) and Venus (♀), acting as the Sulphur (🜍), have the upper hand, they beget a masculine body, which is called Sol <note>The Sun, representing the gold or "red" stage of the work.</note>. And Mercury (☿) is helpful to both parts, for he is the Mediator, who unites and encompasses both in himself; he is the man, and also the woman, as one wishes. 

When those of old wished to instruct their successors through writings, they had to devise something that could be compared with such things, and give these "children" names according to their nature. When the matter is still unripe, sour, deadly, and poisonous, it must be called Snake, Dragon, Basilisk, Poison, Dragon's Blood, Toad, or Adder. When it possesses sharpness and medicinal power, it is called Milk, Wine, and Blood. But when it has become heavenly, it is the food of the gods: Nectar and Ambrosia. If it tinctures <note>To "tincture" means to fundamentally transform or color another metal into gold or silver.</note> or is of a metallic nature, it takes the names of the planets, as they grow according to their degrees.

### LXXXII. How can so many things come from this leaden matter or mineral, which is nonetheless unclean, poisonous, volatile, lowly, and despised?

**Answer:** This <term>Matter</term> <note>original: "Materia," the raw material used in the alchemical work.</note> is the "flower of the earth" and indeed of all metals; it carries much arsenical poison with it, yet it is not as poisonous therein as in <term>Cobalt water-pyrite</term> <note>original: "Cobold Wasser-Kieß," likely cobalt-bearing arsenopyrite.</note> or <term>red silver ore</term> <note>original: "roth gülden Erz," the mineral pyrargyrite.</note>, because the latter still has a terrible <term>Acid</term> <note>original: "Acidum," used here to mean a corrosive mineral spirit.</note> with it, which causes it to act vehemently. If an animal body receives it into the stomach, it creates black necrotic spots where it settles and causes death. When it is cast upon <term>Venus</term> <note>Symbol ♀; refers to Copper.</note>, it turns the copper white, but it immediately tarnishes in the air and becomes black. 

By contrast, our arsenic from lead is somewhat milder and sweeter; it can be taken in small doses for chest illnesses resulting from <term>tenacious fluids</term> <note>original: "zähen Flüssen," likely referring to thick phlegm or congestion.</note>, as it immediately causes a <term>fermentation</term> and removes such fluids through an <term>emetic</term> <note>original: "Vomitiv," a substance that induces vomiting.</note>, though it mostly carries them out from below. In such cases, nothing but death and instantaneous suffocation would otherwise be hoped for. It is taken only in doses of half to one full grain, and is well-corrected by <term>Spirit of Wine</term> <note>original: "Spiritum Vini," high-proof alcohol or ethanol.</note>. 

Furthermore, this substance does not turn <term>Venus</term> <note>Copper</note> black; however, once it has been turned into an oil, it becomes the <term>Basilisk</term> <note>A legendary creature whose gaze or breath was lethal; in alchemy, it refers to a highly potent and dangerous substance.</note> and is far more poisonous than before—it is a <term>tincturing poison</term> <note>original: "venenum tingens," a poison capable of staining or transforming the nature of other substances.</note>. ### LXXXV. But how can his mercury perform such a wonderful dissolution, and how does that happen?

**Answer.** We see this in common **mercury** <note>☿</note>, how it—as a dry body—**dissolves** <note>original: "solvirt"</note> metals; but even more so when it is **sublimated through salts** <note>original: "durch Salia sublimirt"</note>. However, when the **corrosive sublimate** <note>Mercury(II) chloride</note> is sublimated, dissolved through **spirit of salt** <note>original: "Spiritum Salis," now known as hydrochloric acid</note>, and finally rises over as an oil, it dissolves even better. So too our **mercury**, when it is the **Maiden’s Milk** <note>original: "Jungfer-Milch," a poetic term for a white, milky alchemical solvent.</note>, it dissolves the **Moon** <note>Silver, represented by the symbol ☽</note>, stays with it, and becomes silver. Common mercury does not do this; although it may **precipitate** <note>original: "præcipitirt"</note> with the silver, when it is placed upon the **cupel** <note>original: "Capelle," a porous ceramic bowl used in assaying to separate precious metals from impurities like lead.</note>, it departs again, and one has no more silver than before. Why? It only clings to the **Moon** <note>Silver</note> from the outside and has no **lunar sulfur** with it as ours does. Because our mercury softens the silver, crawls—so to speak—into all its veins, ennobles itself with it, and because it is of one essence (or its "first water"), it stays with the silver and thereby becomes a permanent **body of the Moon** <note>original: "Corpus ☽," meaning a stable, fixed silver.</note>. But our **double mercury** is far more exalted and in much greater power: when it has been sublimated into the **foliated earth** <note>original: "Terra foliata," a stage where the matter is purified into leaf-like crystals.</note>, it is the **full moon**, the **white earth** <note>represented by the symbol ♁</note> which **radically dissolves** <note>original: "radicaliter solvirt," meaning to break down to the very root.</note> all metals. The true **universal solvent** <note>original: "Menstruum universale"</note> is the **star** <note>represented by the symbol *; likely the "Starry Regulus of Antimony," a star-shaped crystalline structure seen as a sign of purity.</note> which crawls into the metals, seeks the heart, and makes them volatile or fixed according to how one directs the work: white on the outside, blood-red on the inside.

### 89. The hard, fierce dragon Python is indeed the double Mercury; but what is Phoebus's arrow?

**Answer:** Yes, it is the scaly dragon, the **foliated earth** which shines like fish eyes and shimmers like fish eyes. Phoebus’s arrow—which is also called **Delius** <note>A title for Apollo, born on the island of Delos</note>—is the poisonous, smoking **oil of Saturn** <note>original symbol: ♄</note>, the "Sun" that this Old Man held within his body. This is also called the **blood of young children**, in which the **Sun** and **Moon** <note>Gold and Silver, or the masculine and feminine principles</note> are accustomed to bathe. This is **Saturn’s scythe**, with which he cuts off the wings of **Mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note>; that is, the matter is "fixed" <note>rendered solid and no longer volatile</note>. At this point, the glass vessel must not be opened, nor should anything be added or removed, until the **Stone of the First Order** is finished. For at this stage, there is no feeding or imbibing <note>adding liquid</note> as there was previously in the preparation of this Mercury; rather, it is its **fixing** and **calcination** <note>reduction to a powder through heat</note>. For this reason, it is called the **Hermetic Seal**.

### XCV. I would like to have the true <term>Saturn ♄</term> <note>symbol for Saturn, which in alchemy represents lead and the starting material of the "Great Work"</note> explained even better?

**Answer:** Saturn [♄] is a son of Heaven and Earth, of the goddess Vesta, and the husband of his sister Opis; he is the helping and sustaining power of all things, the ancient Demogorgon <note>a primordial deity in alchemical mythology, representing the dark, chaotic origin of matter</note>, who swallows his children and gives them back again. He is painted with white-gray hair, in his hand a sickle or scythe, and a snake whose head bites its tail <note>the Ouroboros, representing the cyclic nature of the universe and the continuous recycling of matter</note>, indicating his self-helping and regenerating nature. ### * XCIX. How is the multiplying ferment made?

Answer: The **sublimated mercury** <note>original: ☿ ſublimatum</note> of the seven nights is dissolved in its own <term>Aqua Fortis</term> <note>original: AF.; literally "Strong Water," usually referring to nitric acid</note> as an oil or vapor, and drawn off from this * <note>The asterisk likely refers to sal ammoniac or a specific "star" of matter mentioned in earlier steps</note>; this is the true philosophical <term>Aqua Regia</term> <note>original: AR.; "Royal Water," a potent acid mixture capable of dissolving noble metals</note> and the **mineral bath**. When the mercury has been turned into an oil, or into a water that does not wet the hands, it is the true **graduation oil** <note>a substance used to "grade" or elevate the properties and color of a metal</note>; it is the bath in which the **Man and Woman** <note>alchemical symbols for the active/sulfuric and passive/mercurial principles</note> can bathe themselves, for it dissolves and joins them together.

### C. What is done after that?

Answer: One makes the second composition, namely that of the **Stone**.

### CI. How is that same thing made?

Answer: The **mercury** <note>original: ☿</note> must be made "fixed" <note>rendered stable so that it no longer evaporates under heat</note>; then it is our **white mercury**.

### CII. Is this then the Stone, when they say:

**106.** <note>original: CVI.</note> What does one do next with this **Lion** <term>♌</term>?

**Answer:** The **Lion** <term>♌</term> is the **Sun's** <note>The Sun represents Gold or the "Sulfur" of the philosophers</note> own house, and it must be heated by the **Sun** so that the Sun passes through this sign in its exaltation <note>In astrology, planets have signs where they are most powerful, known as "exaltation." But first, this **Lion** <term>♌</term> must be heated through the air or heaven, so that it can devour the bright **Sun**—that is, to take it into its house.

### 107. Why are these two fiery solvents <term>menstrua</term> <note>original: "Menstrua"; in alchemy, a "menstruum" is a solvent or "liquid of life" capable of dissolving solid matter</note> called the Lion <term>♌</term>?

### CXIII. **What then is the Philosophers' Vinegar <term>Acetum philosophorum</term>?**

It is the **Virgin’s Milk** <term>Lac Virginis</term> <note>A term for a corrosive or white mercurial water used to dissolve substances without destroying their essential "seed."</note>.

### CXIV. **What then is the preparation of the Eagle's Glue?**

**Answer:** It is the making of our slimy water, once it has been coagulated into a crystal.

### CXV. **What then is Antimony <term>Antimonium</term> or the Lead of the Philosophers <term>Plumbum Philosophorum</term>?**

**Answer:** It is the red **Antimony** <note>original symbol: ♁</note>, and the **Lily of the Ancients**. The **Sulfur** <note>original symbol: ‡</note> is of two kinds: one is the common black, the other is the female, which is white, called **leaden marcasite** <term>marcafitta plumbea</term> <note>A term used for various metallic minerals; here it refers to a specific white stage of the base material.</note>.

### CXV. **How have they described the work that should be undertaken with it?**

**Answer:** They have described it thus: one should dissolve it in distilled vinegar—which, however, is not vinegar. <note>Alchemists frequently used common names like "vinegar" or "water" to refer to their secret corrosive solvents, warning the reader not to take the terms literally.</note>

### CXVI. How does one make the **Antimony** <note>original symbol: ♁</note> Blood?

**Answer:** One must pour one’s own **Philosophers' Vinegar** onto the red-calcined **Antimony** <note>original symbol: ♁</note>; it will then turn a deep red. This is distilled gently, and the blessed oil of this mineral comes over in blood-red droplets like real blood, to which the treasures of the whole world cannot be compared.

### CXVII. How then does one dissolve **Silver** <note>original symbol: ☽</note> in the philosophical manner?

**Answer:** It is dissolved in six parts of our calcining water, the **Virgin's Milk** <term>Lac Virginis</term>, and gently distilled until it appears as an oil. The green water is thereafter dissolved and distilled again; in three repetitions, the **Silver** <note>original symbol: ☽</note> is turned to oil. Thereupon our **solvent spirit of wine** <term>spiritus vini solventis</term> increases in strength, so that it takes the **Sulphur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> of the **Silver** into itself, which one can then separate and reunite.

### CXVIII. How then does one dissolve **Gold** <note>original symbol: ☉</note>?

**Answer:** One dissolves it in the red **Virgin's Milk** and **cohobates** <term>the process of repeatedly distilling a liquid off the solid matter from which it was just distilled</term> it until it is turned into oil. Or, one separates the **Sulphur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> from it using **solvent wine** <term>vinum solvens</term> and joins them together again. Alternatively, one dissolves them both through our **Water of Life** <term>Aqua-vit / Aqua Vitae</term>, which consists of spirit, soul, and body.

### CXIX. What then is the **Burning Water** <note>original: *Aqua ardens*</note>, or **Water of Life** <note>original: *Aqua-Vitæ*</note>?

**Answer:** It is neither brandy nor **spirit of wine** <note>original: *Spiritus-Vini*</note>, but our **Water of Life**, which makes [the matter] living, which is the **Spirit of Mercury** <term>original symbol: ☿</term> and has its origin in **Saturn** <term>original symbol: ♄; often referring to lead or the "prima materia"</term>.

### CXX. What then is the **philosophical fire**; is it of one kind, or is it understood in many ways?

**Answer:** Firstly, there is the **glowing white fire**, which is also called **Mary's Bath** <term>Balneum Mariæ; a gentle water bath used for heating</term>, as well as our **horse dung** <note>A term for a gentle, steady heat produced by fermenting manure, used for slow digestion of substances</note> and **secret furnace**, which must be applied to its own vessel. This vessel is called the **green vessel** <term>vas viride</term> of **Saturn** <term>original symbol: ♄</term>. In this fire, **Pontanus** <note>Johannes Pontanus, a famous alchemist who wrote about the "Secret Fire," claiming he discovered it only after failing two hundred times</note> erred more than two hundred times, even though he worked with the correct **Material** <note>original: *Materia*</note>. 2. We have the **fire against nature**, which burns more fiercely than the fires of hell; this is the **Stygian Water** <note>original: *Aqua Stygia*; typically a corrosive mineral acid</note>. 3. We have a fire that is a **yellow Sulphur** <term>original symbol: 🜍</term> **Oil**. 4. We have our **Solar Fire**, the **glowing red** one.

### CXXI. What is the **Sulphur** <term>original symbol: 🜍</term> of nature?

**Answer:** It is our **white Sulphur**.

### CXXII. What does one do with it?

**Answer:** It must be **dissolved** <note>original: *solvirt*</note> into oil, so that it becomes the **incombustible oil**.

### CXXIII. What more is done with it? Is it all made into **Oil**, or only a part?

**Answer:** One part is made **fixed** <term>stable under heat; non-volatile</term>, and the other is **dissolved** <note>original: *solvirt*</note> into **Oil**.

### CXXIV. With what is it made **fixed**?

**Answer:** With its own **Fire** <term>original symbol: 🜂</term>, or fire that does not burn the hands <note>A reference to a "secret" or "inner" heat that provides transformative power without the destructive force of common fire</note>.

### CXXV. What does the **Stone** **tincture** <term>transform or color</term>?

**Answer:** It is capable of **tincturing** the whole world.

### CXXVI. Why then should and can one not make the **Great Work** <term>the creation of the Philosopher's Stone</term> from **Gold** <term>original symbol: ☉</term> and **Silver**, since most have made their **Stone** from gold and silver?

**Answer:** Because it is not possible to make blossoms out of ripe fruits again, or a child out of a man; one cannot bring him back into his mother’s womb to be born anew. But **Art** <note>The "Alchemical Art," which seeks to assist or accelerate natural processes</note> is permitted to promote the growth of the raw and unripe, to ennoble it and lead it to the highest stage, which Nature cannot do. However, because many could not find the **Great Work** in the form of the **philosophical Gold** <term>original symbol: ☉</term> and **Silver** <term>original symbol: ☽</term>, they made their stones from common gold and silver; they had to use the **Menstrua** <term>powerful alchemical solvents</term>, as well as coloring wet and dry spirits, upon common gold and silver, to color them within and bring them to a **Tincture**...

### CXXVII. Can one also make **tincturing stones** from **minerals**?

**Answer:** Yes, especially from **Antimony** <term>original symbol: ♁; often called "the wolf" in alchemy for its ability to "consume" other metals</term>, by way of the **wet and dry paths**, when the **Virgin’s Milk** <note>original: *Jungfer-Milch*; a term for a potent philosophical solvent or corrosive liquid</note> dissolves it, or our **dry Mercury** <term>original symbol: ☿</term> is united with it for seven nights; then they both dissolve each other so that they become one and rise up like the beautiful **Dawn** <note>original: *Morgenröthe*; a reference to the alchemical stage of reddening or the approaching completion of the work</note>. ### CXXVIII. How can this **Water** do such great things, that it can even ennoble raw and unripe minerals and transform them into magnificent **tinctures**?

### CXXIX. What then is the Demogorgon?

**Answer:** The **Demogorgon** <note>A mysterious primal deity often cited in alchemical texts as the "father of all things" or the raw, chaotic source of nature</note> is our **Ancient One**, who holds all of nature within himself; he is also our **Dragon**. He contains a central fire and vapor within him—namely the **Spirit of the World** <note>original: *Spiritum mundi*; a universal life force or essence</note> or **Mercury** <term>original symbol: ☿</term>. He releases this from his heart; likewise, a pure **Earth**, which must be prepared by artful means.

### CXXX. What then is the "fire against nature"?

**Answer:** I have said it before: it is the corrosive, stinking water, the **Stygian Water** <note>original: *Aqua Stygia*; named after the River Styx in the underworld, this refers to a powerful acid or solvent used to dissolve metals</note>, in which the **Dragon** is killed and the **Mercury** <term>original symbol: ☿</term> is made **fixed** <note>to "fix" a substance is to turn it from a volatile, evaporating state into a solid, stable one</note>. It is the scythe of the flying **Saturn** <term>original symbol: ♄; representing lead and the principle of time or death</term>, with which he cuts off the wings of **Mercury** <term>original symbol: ☿</term>. This is the hellish fire that **calcines** <note>reduces to a powder through heat</note> and transforms it into a fixed body, turning the **Mercury of the Philosophers** into a fixed **Precipitate**.

### CXXXI. But why should this fire "fix" the Mercury, when it was stated earlier that it should be hardened in the Earth and coagulated therein?

**Answer:** Previously, the slaggy and watery **Mercury** <term>original symbol: ☿</term> had to be hardened by its own **Earth** or **Salt** through the **Iron Salt** <note>likely referring to vitriol or a martial salt</note>. For every Earth has the power to harden its own **Mercury**; and when it takes such dry Earth or Salt into itself, its moisture is dried up so that it is no longer running, but instead becomes numb, hardened, and **coagulated**. For it must join itself with its own fixed body...

### CXL. **How does one turn the fixed Mercury <note>original symbol: ☿</note> of the Philosophers <note>original: *Philosophorum*</note>, or this precipitate, or stone, into oil?**

He has found the **Hermetic Good** <note>The Philosopher's Stone or Universal Medicine.</note>; now he must serve **God** alone, and not forget his poor neighbor, nor close his heart against him.

## CLXXVIII. How is it made?

Answer: Take **Antimony** <note>original: "♁"</note> calcined until yellow and the best **Vitriol** <note>original: "🜔"</note>, **equal parts of each** <note>original: "ana"</note>; from these an **Aqua Fortis** is distilled without the addition of water. One dissolves the salt from the **Residue** <note>original: "Caput Mortuum"</note> in distilled wine-vinegar, lets it evaporate to dryness, then pours the **Aqua Fortis** upon it. One draws it off strongly from its salt until the **Retort** <term>Retort</term> <note>A glass vessel with a long downward-pointing neck used for distilling liquids</note> glows. Into one pound of this **Aqua Fortis**—drawn from its **Residue**—one throws 4 **Lot** <note>original: "Loth"; a unit of weight roughly equal to 1/2 ounce or 15 grams</note> of **Corrosive Sublimate**, and 3 **Lot** of **Salmiac** <note>original: "*"</note>; distill it over, and thus the **Salmiac** and **Sublimate** are separated from one another, and [it becomes] a magnificent **Solvent** <term>Menstruum</term> <note>A liquid used to dissolve a solid; the "philosophical" solvent of the alchemists</note>. Into this, pour an equal amount of **Oil of Mercury** <note>original: "Oleum ☿"</note>; distill it over again, then it is ready and always to be used. It possesses very great powers,

### CLXXIX. I would also like to hear about the Corallatum of Paracelsus, with which he is said to have performed so many wonder-cures?

**Answer.** He describes it himself like this: That you take the **Liquor of the Eagle** <note>original: "Liquorem Aquil."; likely a reference to Sal Ammoniac or a specific mercurial solvent</note> and dry it out. Afterward, take the prepared **Liquor of Antimony** <note>original: "Liquorem ♁. Præparati"</note>, soak it, and—just as the process is for **calcined Tartar**—draw off its **Spirit** <note>the volatile essence</note> until it is fully extracted: thus is the **Corallatum** <note>A red powder, usually a form of mercuric oxide, named for its coral-like color</note> prepared. Here, by the "Liquor of the Eagle," he means the **wet virgin Mercury** <note>pure, native mercury found in the earth</note>, which should be dried and then covered with the **Liquor of Antimony**. This is repeated until it all remains upon it and has become coral-red. This can only be performed by those who have learned to **separate the elements** in the **Philosophical Work** <note>The "Great Work" of alchemy, or the creation of the Philosopher's Stone</note>, and who can prepare the **Mercury of the Sages**. However, because he learned to make another Corallatum, I will set that down as well; it is a description of a **precipitate** <term>Precipitate</term> <note>A solid that settles out of a liquid solution</note> for the **French Disease** <note>original: "*Morbo Gallico*"; the historical term for Syphilis</note> and other foul sicknesses. He describes it with these words: The mercury should be **calcined** <term>Calcined</term> <note>Heated to a high temperature to drive off volatile parts or reduce to a powder</note> in **Aqua Fortis** <term>Aqua Fortis</term> <note>Nitric acid</note>; then, a **grading Aqua Fortis** <note>A fortified or concentrated nitric acid</note> is drawn off from it 5 or more times, until the precipitate takes on a pleasing color and is a beautiful red; then, a **rectified brandy** <note>Distilled alcohol</note> is drawn off from it...

### CLXXXI. Making Salt of Tartar Volatile

->I would also like to know this:<-

Answer: This happens in various ways. The first, which pleases me best, happens in this manner: A very **fiery salt of tartar** is **dissolved in the air** <note>original: "an der Lufft solvirt"; the process of deliquescence, where a dry salt absorbs enough atmospheric moisture to become liquid</note>. Upon this is poured **volatile oil of turpentine** in a wide **sugar-glass** <note>a wide-mouthed glass jar used in pharmacies</note>, and it is stirred together often. Thus, the fatty oil of turpentine takes the fiery salt into itself, and from both a **thick soap** is made; one oil dissolves the other. When they have now become **one body**, and no more moisture is to be seen, one distills it. ### CLXXXV. From what, then, is the animal stone made?

**Answer.** From the great animal, man; likewise from **phosphorus** <note>In early alchemy, phosphorus was often distilled from human urine, thus categorizing it as an "animal" substance</note>. These have great utility in medicine, and many curious things can be made with them; both can be used for the mineral kingdom.

### CLXXXVI. Do these stones then not serve for the great Universal Stone, or do they not belong to it?

**Answer.** One must not blend or mix one with the other; like stays with like, and brings forth fruit according to its own kind. Whoever acts against this creates a **monstrosity** <note>German: "Mißgeburt"</note> and breeds a mule; just as when a horse and a donkey mate, this infertile animal is produced. For the **Mineral Stone** <note>The alchemical stone intended for the transmutation of metals</note>, nothing may be added except a mineral, which possesses everything within itself to make itself perfect. He who does otherwise does violence to Nature and will find himself deceived in the end, for he will not obtain what he desired and hoped for.

### CXCV. How does one then dissolve this solvent? <term>Menstruum</term> <note>A "menstruum" is an alchemical term for a solvent used to extract the essence or "soul" of a substance.</note>

Answer: The **pearls** are crushed and dissolved in **Virgin’s Milk** <term>Jungfer-Milch</term> <note>In alchemy, this usually refers to a white liquid or a specific mercurial water used as a solvent, rather than literal milk.</note>; upon this, one can pour a **spirit of wine** <term>Spiritum vini</term> <note>original: "Spiritum vini"; high-proof alcohol or ethanol used for extraction.</note> and digest <note>to heat gently over a period of time to encourage dissolution</note> it. Afterward, distill it over, and a "pearl-milk" will come across, and finally a yellow oil. Both of these are for use in cases of stroke <note>paralysis or seizures</note> and loss of speech, to restore them; a **heart-tonic** <term>Cordiale</term> <note>original: "Cordiale"; a medicine intended to invigorate the heart and spirit.</note> like this is not to be found, even after the Universal <note>Referring to the "Universal Medicine" or Philosopher's Stone.</note>.

### CXCVI. How does one then dissolve the metals in it?

Answer: This breaking down <note>original: "Zerschmertzung"</note> does not happen violently, but gradually; they melt away in it and become oil and salves: the **Gold** <note>symbol: ☉</note> into red water, and the **Silver** <note>symbol: ☽</note> into white. The metals may also first be brought into a **calx** <term>Kalk</term> <note>the fine powder or ash remaining after a metal has been roasted or oxidized by fire.</note>.

## CXCVIII. How then is this understood, when they say this stone is everything, and is also nothing?

**Answer:** This is the meaning: It is everything if one knows its preparation, and it is also nothing if one does not understand the work. Even if one understands the <term>Authors</term> <note>original: "Auctores"; refers to the established alchemical authorities and classical writers.</note> well and knows the entire work perfectly in one's head, as soon as one undertakes the <term>Practice</term> <note>original: "Praxin"</note>, such secret knots arise to be untied, and things are seen that bewitch the sight, as it were, so that one does not know which way is out. There are certain limits, times, and hours determined by nature which one must not exceed. I have indeed indicated all and each of these in my previous little <term>treatises</term> <note>original: "Tractätlein"</note> and also here, and discovered everything as clear as day; yet it will still be difficult if someone wishes to run up, as it were, with an unwashed mouth <note>A common German idiom of the era meaning to approach something with a lack of respect or proper preparation.</note> and kiss the naked <term>Diana</term> <note>In alchemical allegory, Diana (the moon goddess) represents the "Lunar" or silver stage of the work. To see her "naked" refers to the revelation of the secret "matter" of the Stone, a sight said to be dangerous for the unprepared.</note>. This is no work, as they say, for peasants like greasing a wagon; one must be well-experienced in the fire, have burnt one's fingers, and have read many a fine book, otherwise he will fall short by a wide margin.

...burns, as in strong <term>Spirit of Wine</term> <note>original: "Spiritu vini"; highly concentrated alcohol used as a solvent.</note>, for the Air is well <term>rectified</term> <note>Purified or refined through distillation.</note>, which takes into itself the Red <term>Lion's</term> <note>symbol: ♌; the "Red Lion" often refers to the secret sulfur of the philosophers or a specific stage of the chemical work.</note> Blood, and the colors of a **Rainbow** appear when this <term>Gold</term> <note>symbol: ☉</note> enters into its first essence.
